RNA viruses emerged as dominant players within the bloom, with fluctuations of putative diatom-infecting RNA viruses across intracellular and extracellular fractions revealing sequential waves of active virus infection that were consistent with virus-mediated diatom mortality. Correlation and codon usage analyses further implicated specific diatom taxa as putative hosts for the identified RNA viruses. Rather than a uniform 'boom and bust', the spring diatom bloom comprised a mosaic of overlapping successional waves of diatom and viral taxa unfolding on daily timescales. These findings support RNA viruses as drivers of diatom turnover, advancing our understanding of how viruses temporally structure diverse diatom assemblages and the biogeochemical trajectory of diatom blooms in marine systems.

title: Brain region-specific lesions in the early AIDS monkey model.
abstract: Brain lesions show pronounced regional heterogeneity during chronic or advanced human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection; however, the regional neuropathogenesis during the acute phase remains unclear. By establishing an acute simian immunodeficiency virus (SIV)-infection model in rhesus macaques, we found acute infection-induced robust neuroinflammation and neuronal damage. Compared with the cerebral cortex, subcortical nuclei displayed earlier and more severe neuronal degeneration and loss of Nissl bodies, accompanied by greater upregulation of immune-related genes. Although SIV RNA loads in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and plasma were strongly correlated and peaked during acute infection, brain tissues showed no evidence of early viral reservoir establishment. The viral transactivator Tat persisted in CSF and was broadly distributed throughout the brain via passive diffusion along perivascular spaces. Similar transcriptional and inflammatory profiles were observed between macaques with acute infection and mice receiving intracisternal Tat infusions identified Tat as a principal mediator of early SIV-induced neurotoxicity. Microglia in a primed immune-vigilant state exhibited considerable enrichment in subcortical nuclei, driving exaggerated responses to Tat exposure and resulting in region-specific neuropathological outcomes. Collectively, these findings delineate the spatiotemporal landscape of acute HIV/SIV-induced brain injury and establish viral Tat as a mechanistic driver of acute neuropathogenesis.

title: An Isotope-Induced Polarity Bias in Electrospray Ionization Mass Spectrometry.
abstract: Heavy water (D2O) is commonly used as a solvent additive in electrospray ionization-mass spectrometry (ESI-MS) to probe biomolecular interactions under the assumption that isotopic substitution does not significantly affect the ionization process. However, D2O differs measurably from H2O in several physicochemical properties, which can influence ionization across biomolecular classes. Here, we systematically investigate how D2O influences native ESI across biomolecular classes and show that D2O introduces a pronounced, polarity-dependent detection bias which can suppress the signal of proteins and peptides in negative ion mode relative to other classes of biomolecules. Protein signal suppression is mitigated by reducing primary ESI droplet size or adding volatile ammonium salts, implicating altered droplet evolution and salt retention in D2O. Its magnitude is strongly dependent on analyte acidity: basic and moderately acidic proteins are most affected, whereas extremely negatively charged proteins, RNA, and polysaccharides remain largely unaffected. Signal loss also correlates with extensive sodium adduction and peak splitting rather than impaired charging. Exploiting this selectivity, we demonstrate controlled switching between peptide and RNA detection in a coacervate-based cellular delivery system. These findings reveal an unexpected solvent-dependent bias in negative-mode native MS measurements which can be exploited for experimental design.

title: Catalytic Hairpin Assembly-Aided CRISPR/Cas-SERS for Nucleic Acid Detection Enhanced by Multiple Catalytic Amplification.
abstract: This study established a surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) detection method based on the catalytic hairpin assembly (CHA) reaction combined with clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats and its associated proteins (CRISPR/Cas), integrated with the guanine-quadruplexes/Hemin (G4/Hemin) catalytic amplification effect, which is available for identifying a typical indicator for genetically modified crops, the 35S promoter from the cauliflower mosaic virus (CaMV35S). Target CaMV35S-derived RNA (CaMV35S RNA) triggers the CHA reaction, yielding a double-stranded DNA product (C1/C2) that is recognized by CRISPR RNA (crRNA), thereby activating the trans-cleavage activity of Cas12a. A magnetic bead-based nanoprobe was fabricated by linking the hybridization chain reaction (HCR) product to the magnetic bead. This probe can fold into repeated G4 units under a specific potassium ion concentration to enable a high loading of Hemin, thereby providing strong peroxidase-like catalytic activity for 3,3',5,5'-tetra-methyl-benz-idine (TMB). In a positive trial, the 35S RNA initiates CHA, and the CHA product activates Cas12a, disrupting the HCR products on the magnetic bead probe, preventing the G4 structure formation, accordingly yielding a weak SERS signal from TMB. In contrast, a negative trial fails to activate Cas12a, and the probe retains its nanoenzyme activity, resulting in a strong SERS signal from the produced oxTMB. Owing to the collateral trans-cleavage activity of Cas12a and the high peroxidase-like nanozyme activity of G4/Hemin, this method achieves the highly sensitive SERS detection of genetically modified samples without target gene preamplification.

title: Cellular Morphological Profiling of PROTAC Degraders of the m6A RNA Methyltransferase METTL3.
abstract: Methylation of N6-adenosine is the most abundant RNA modification, which is mainly installed on mRNA by the methyltransferase METTL3-METTL14 complex. Dysregulation of the catalytic activity of METTL3 has been associated with many human diseases, especially in acute myeloid leukemia and other cancers. Therefore, both monovalent small-molecule inhibitors and bivalent heterobifunctional proteolysis-targeting chimera (PROTAC) degraders have been pursued to address METTL3 for therapeutic development. In this study, we report the structure-based design and synthesis of new METTL3-targeting PROTACs, as well as the first application of unbiased morphological profiling of the obtained METTL3 PROTACs in the cell painting assay to obtain phenotypic characterization data for the further development of METTL3 PROTAC degraders.

title: Mediator complex: the unsung hero of hematopoiesis.
abstract: Hematopoiesis is a hierarchical process governed by complex transcriptional networks that dictate the self-renewal and lineage-specific differentiation of hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs). While not the sole central regulator, the Mediator complex plays a crucial role in this landscape as a highly conserved multi-protein assembly that transmits signals from enhancer-bound transcription factors to RNA polymerase II. Through its distinct structural modules, particularly the cyclin-dependent kinase module (CKM), Mediator acts as a crucial regulator of transcriptional initiation and elongation. Emerging evidence underscores the Mediator's indispensable role in normal blood cell development and hematological pathologies. Genetic ablation of specific Mediator subunits severely compromises HSC stemness, impairs erythroid maturation, and disrupts embryonic circulatory development. Furthermore, Mediator dysregulation is intricately linked to the pathogenesis of malignant hematological disorders, especially leukemias. This review synthesizes current knowledge regarding the Mediator complex's function in embryonic and adult hematopoiesis, with a primary focus on human and murine erythropoiesis. We critically examine the molecular mechanisms underlying hematological diseases driven by Mediator dysfunction and highlight the key complex's components important for different blood pathologies. Finally, we outline future perspectives on targeting specific Mediator components, such as the CDK8/19 kinases, as promising therapeutic strategies for treating Mediator-dependent hematological diseases.

title: CDSeq2 integrates individual-level cell-type expression deconvolution with recoverability-guided prioritization
abstract: CDSeq2 combines reference-informed Bayesian deconvolution with gene-type prioritization for individual-level expression analysis from bulk RNA sequencing. Brain benchmarks showed accurate RNA-fraction estimates and expression recovery comparable to BayesPrism in excitatory neurons. Prioritization enriched accurately recovered profiles and supported continuous-phenotype and cell-type-specific expression quantitative trait locus (eQTL) analyses, with the strongest application evidence in excitatory neurons. Forty independently generated synthetic cohorts with local linkage disequilibrium evaluated a frozen scorer. In the principal stronger-effect setting, retaining 40% of candidate profiles increased eQTL precision from 77.6% to 92.6%. CDSeq2 delivers complete expression estimates with optional prioritization to support focused biological follow-up.

title: Mechanisms of Spns2 in regulating neuroinflammatory activation of microglia after cerebral ischemia in rats.
abstract: Microglia, the resident innate immune cells of the brain, maintain central nervous system homeostasis but can also mediate inflammatory injury after ischemic stroke. Following ischemia, microglia can adopt pro-inflammatory M1- or reparative M2-like state; thus, regulating the balance between these phenotypes may be therapeutically relevant. Sphingosine-1-phosphate signaling regulates immune responses, angiogenesis, and endothelial barrier integrity. Enhanced sphingosine-1-phosphate signaling in activated microglia after ischemic injury may amplify inflammatory cascades. However, strategies targeting sphingosine-1-phosphate signaling are constrained by the heterogeneous expression of sphingosine-1-phosphate receptors. Spinster homolog 2 (Spns2), a sphingosine-1-phosphate exporter, may provide an alternative target, although its role in ischemic stroke remains unclear. To investigate the role of Spns2 in post-ischemic neuroinflammation, middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion was induced in Spns2-deficient (Spns2-/-) and wild-type rats. BV2 microglial cells exposed to oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation were used as an in vitro model. Spns2 mRNA expression in the peri-infarct penumbra increased after middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion and peaked at 24 hours. Compared with wild-type rats, Spns2-/- rats showed lower neurological deficit scores, improved motor performance, and smaller infarct volumes. In the peri-infarct penumbra, Spns2 deficiency was associated with decreased expression of pro-inflammatory markers, increased expression of anti-inflammatory markers, and attenuated microglia-associated NOD-like receptor pyrin domain-containing protein 3 (NLRP3) inflammasome signaling. In BV2 cells, Spns2 knockdown produced similar changes in inflammatory-marker expression and reduced oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation-induced NLRP3 inflammasome-associated signaling and oxidative stress. Spns2 knockdown reduced extracellular sphingosine-1-phosphate levels in BV2-cell culture supernatants, whereas exogenous sphingosine-1-phosphate supplementation increased the expression of inflammasome-associated inflammatory mediators in Spns2-knockdown BV2 cells. RNA sequencing identified Itga5 upregulation in Spns2-/- rats and showed that differentially expressed genes between Spns2-/- and wild-type rats were enriched in the phosphoinositide 3-kinase/protein kinase B (Akt) signaling pathway. Increased Akt phosphorylation in Spns2-/- rats was further confirmed by western blotting. These findings indicate that Spns2 deficiency limits sphingosine-1-phosphate export and attenuates microglia-associated neuroinflammation after ischemic stroke. Itga5 upregulation and increased Akt phosphorylation may be associated with this neuroprotective effect. Collectively, our results provide a basis for further investigation of the Spns2-sphingosine-1-phosphate axis in ischemic stroke.

title: The lncRNA Statera regulates synaptogenesis by repressing the retrotransposon copia in Drosophila.
abstract: Retrotransposons are mobile genetic elements that can impair genome integrity, and their insertions and dysregulation have been implicated in various diseases. However, growing evidence suggests that retrotransposons may play important physiological roles. At the Drosophila larval neuromuscular junction (NMJ), the ViSyToR (Viral Synaptic Transfer of RNA) pathway requires the active retrotransposon copia as a key negative regulator of synaptogenesis. Here, we identify a long non-coding RNA, Statera ( Stae ), as a regulator of copia , initially discovered through its physical association with the Copia protein. Stae is highly expressed in the central nervous system and body wall muscles of Drosophila larvae. CRISPR knockout or RNAi knockdown of Stae leads to a general decrease of bouton number at the NMJ, indicating its role in promoting synaptogenesis. Furthermore, copia is highly upregulated in Stae mutants, suggesting that Stae functions to repress copia . Mechanistically, Stae reduces copia RNA stability and limits copia DNA copy number. Additional knockdown of copia in motor neuron-specific Stae RNAi animals rescues the abnormal NMJ morphology. Together, our findings reveal an unexpected role for a long non-coding RNA in promoting synaptogenesis by repressing a retrotransposon.

title: N 6 -methyladenosine regulates Influenza A virus mRNA stability yet is rarely found on genomic RNA.
abstract: Previous studies have found widespread N 6 -methyladenosine (m 6 A methylation) on all forms of Influenza A virus (IAV) RNA, with m 6 A found critical for viral replication, pathogenicity as well as viral RNA packaging. Here we applied the latest quantitative technologies to revisit the methylation landscape on the anti-sense genomic RNA of IAV. Unexpectedly, upon Ultra-Performance Liquid Chromatography-Tandem Mass Spectrometry (UPLC-MS/MS) analysis of IAV virion -extracted genomic RNA, we detected very little m 6 A regardless of production from human cells or chicken eggs. Concordantly, Nanopore direct RNA sequencing also detected an overall low occurrence and stoichiometry (generally <5%) of m 6 A across all viral genomic RNA segments, compared with abundant m 6 A sites on viral mRNAs at ∼20-30% m 6 A. Cross validation with glyoxal- and nitrite-mediated deamination of unmethylated adenosines (GLORI) confirmed multiple m 6 A sites on viral mRNA yet very few m 6 A on the genomic RNA. This paucity of m 6 A on genomic RNA makes it unlikely that m 6 A contributes to viral RNA packaging. Knockdown or pharmacological inhibition of the m 6 A methyltransferase METTL3 as well as the reader protein YTHDF2 both reduced viral mRNA levels and infectious viral particle production, with YTHDF2 promoting viral mRNA stability. Thus, the presence of m 6 A on IAV transcripts is indeed proviral, yet it is the mRNAs instead of genomic RNAs that are methylated at functionally relevant levels. Lastly, we provide proof of concept that a METTL3 small molecule inhibitor can be antiviral, and propose that m 6 A-targeted antivirals would mainly impact the intracellular gene expression phase of IAV replication. Influenza A virus (IAV) is a contagious pathogen that cause seasonal epidemics, and with a large reservoir among birds, has historically switched hosts on multiple occasions and contributed to several pandemics. The rapid evolution of influenza viruses necessitates the development of antivirals that work across virus strains, and one approach is to target host mechanisms that are needed for the replication of a wide range of viruses. The adenosine methylation m 6 A, is present on the RNA of a wide range of viruses including IAV, where it mostly supports viral replication. However, it remains unclear how abundant is m 6 A on IAV RNA. Here, we utilize the latest RNA modification detection methods and found that IAV mRNAs are m 6 A methylated, with little m 6 A on the genomic RNA. We provide evidence that m 6 A on IAV mRNAs may prevent degradation of IAV mRNAs, and provide proof of concept that an m 6 A modification inhibitor can be antiviral against IAV.

title: TransPrimer: A Web-Based Tool for Automated Transcript-Specific RT-PCR/qPCR Primer Design Across Multiple Species.
abstract: Transcript-specific RT-PCR/qPCR primer design is challenging when closely related RNA variants share extensive exonic sequence and differ primarily in exon connectivity. We developed TransPrimer, a web application for automated transcript-specific and pan-transcript primer design. TransPrimer retrieves curated RefSeq protein-coding and non-coding transcripts for six species and compares sibling transcripts to identify discriminating exons and exon-exon junctions (EEJs). The application automatically determines whether transcript specificity can be achieved using exon-targeted primers or requires single- or dual-EEJ strategies. A complementary pan-transcript mode identifies primer pairs that amplify all annotated transcripts of a gene, when feasible, or the largest compatible subset. Junction-spanning primers are evaluated using an arm-specific thermodynamic framework that independently calculates melting temperatures (Tm) for the full primer and its two exon-matching arms using nearest-neighbor thermodynamics and mixed-salt correction. Primer3-based criteria are integrated for partner-primer design and evaluation. User-adjustable reaction parameters, interactive transcript visualization, and custom sequence input support flexible assay development, including novel or externally annotated transcripts. By integrating transcript retrieval, structural comparison, strategy selection, thermodynamic evaluation, and primer generation, TransPrimer reduces manual transcript inspection and facilitates transcript-specific and gene-level RT-PCR/qPCR assay development across diverse transcript architectures.URL: https://transprimer.vercel.app/.

title: Sotagliflozin corrects myocardial phenotype, mitochondrial gene expression and oxidative stress in mice with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.
abstract: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) is associated with mitochondrial dysfunction and oxidative stress. Our goal was to determine the effects of the dual Sodium-Glucose-Linked-Transporter (SGLT) 1 and 2 inhibitor sotagliflozin (SOTA) on myocardial remodeling, diastolic function, mitochondrial gene expression and oxidative stress in mice with HCM due to the tropomyosin E180G mutation (E180G). E180G and non-carrier (NC) mice 7-8 weeks old were randomized to SOTA formulated in the chow (30 mg/kg chow) or control diet (CD) for 8 weeks. Cardiac structure and function were assessed by echocardiography at baseline, and after 4 and 8 weeks of treatment. At 8 weeks mice were sacrificed to assess myocardial histology, RNA expression and oxidative stress. At baseline E180G mice had myocardial hypertrophy and diastolic dysfunction that worsened over the next 8 weeks. In E180G mice, treatment with SOTA for 8 weeks prevented further LV hypertrophy, decreased interstitial fibrosis, normalized diastolic function and decreased atrial size. In E180G hearts mitochondrial gene sets were downregulated and oxidative stress was increased. SOTA treatment upregulated mitochondrial gene sets and prevented the increase in oxidative stress. Upregulated fibrosis gene sets in E180G hearts were not affected by SOTA. In a mouse model of HCM, SOTA exerts beneficial effects on myocardial structure and diastolic function which are associated with restoration of down-regulated mitochondrial gene programs and correction of oxidative stress. SOTA may be of clinical value in the treatment of patients with HCM.

title: Extracellular vesicle cross-linking coupled with solid-phase purification facilitates discovery of ribonucleoprotein complexes assembled on EV RNAs.
abstract: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are fundamental mediators of intercellular communication that transfer macromolecular cargo, including proteins and RNAs, to functionally reprogram recipient cells. However, the molecular processes by which transferred ribonucleoprotein (RNP) complexes engage recipient host machinery to influence cellular behavior are poorly understood, primarily due to a dearth of methods capable of tracking these post-transfer interactions. To address this gap, we developed two complementary chemical biology platforms: EV-CLASP and EV(r)-CLASP. While EV-CLASP maps the native, intra-vesicular RNP landscape packaged within the EV, EV(r)-CLASP captures post-transfer dynamics by identifying the host proteins that directly associate with EV-derived RNAs following cellular uptake. Both approaches leverage metabolic labeling and photo-crosslinking for high-specificity recovery. Donor cells are cultured with 4-thiouridine (4SU) to biosynthetically label newly synthesized RNAs during EV biogenesis. Purified EVs can be crosslinked using 365 nm UV light to capture intra-vesicular RNP composition. Alternatively, 4SU-labeled EVs can be delivered to recipient cells and subsequently crosslinked to identify the primary physical interactions formed within the recipient-cell environment. Crosslinked RNP complexes are isolated under stringent conditions using solid-phase reversible beads to minimize background, followed by quantitative mass spectrometry for protein identification. Together, EV-CLASP and EV(r)-CLASP provide a robust, versatile framework for defining the dynamic RNP assemblies that facilitate extracellular RNA communication, offering a powerful toolkit to uncover novel RNA-associated regulatory networks, therapeutic targets, and biomarkers across diverse biological and disease contexts.

title: Triple-Omics Analysis Unveiled the Neuroprotective Mechanisms of Akkermansia muciniphila in an Environmental Exposure-Linked Mouse Model of Alzheimer's Disease.
abstract: Cadmium (Cd) is an emerging environmental risk factor for cognitive decline and Alzheimer's disease, and few interventions limit its effects on the brain. Akkermansia muciniphila , a human gut commensal, is neuroprotective through mechanisms that remain unclear. Building on our finding that A. muciniphila prevented Cd-induced memory deficits without reducing brain Cd burden (Wang et al., 2026a), we tested whether it reprograms Cd-disrupted hippocampal RNA regulation. Male C57BL/6J mice received A. muciniphila (1×10⁹ CFU, oral gavage, 5 days/week) before and throughout 9 weeks of 3 mg/L CdCl₂ exposure; hippocampi were analyzed by RNA-seq, m⁶A epitranscriptomic profiling, and rMATS-based alternative-splicing analysis. Cd disrupted hippocampal neuropeptide signaling, neuronal excitability, and synaptic plasticity. Co-exposure with A. muciniphila reversed signatures enriched for Nrf2-centered cytoprotective signaling and opposed m⁶A and splicing changes across more than a thousand genes, largely without changes in total mRNA abundance. Restored events converged on machinery governing local translation, calcium-dependent plasticity, and synaptic transmission. Projected onto predicted protein structures, most introduced a premature termination codon predicted to trigger nonsense-mediated decay or edited short loop and linker segments rather than rebuilding folded domains, regulation largely invisible to gene-level expression analysis. Among these, paired events amplifying semaphorin-plexin signaling, an axis linked to oligodendrocyte injury and memory consolidation, were reversed. These findings identify restoration of hippocampal transcript fate and splice-isoform selection as a mechanism potentially underlying A. muciniphila -mediated protection against Cd neurotoxicity, and establish post-transcriptional RNA regulation as a gut-brain target for mitigating environmentally driven neurotoxicity. Cadmium is a widespread environmental contaminant associated with cognitive decline and Alzheimer's disease, and few interventions are available to limit its effects on the brain. This study shows that supplementation with the gut commensal Akkermansia muciniphila reverses Cd-induced changes in hippocampal m⁶A methylation and splice-isoform selection, largely without altering total transcript abundance. These results identify post-transcriptional RNA regulation as a gut-brain target for mitigating environmentally driven neurotoxicity, and show that conventional gene-expression analysis alone would miss most of the protective response.

title: From whole-exome sequencing to functional insight: Characterization of rare germline variants in lung cancer.
abstract: Whole-exome sequencing (WES) has greatly expanded the identification of rare germline variants in hereditary cancer predisposition. However, the interpretation of variants of uncertain significance (VUS), particularly in novel candidate genes, remains a major challenge in lung cancer genetics. To functionally characterize selected germline variants identified by WES in patients with familial or suspected hereditary lung cancer and provide evidence for their prioritization. Three splicing variants in HGS, CDK12, and CEACAM5 genes were investigated by RT-PCR and Sanger sequencing to assess their effect on splicing. Candidate missense variants were analyzed through protein-protein interaction network analysis, gene expression profiling, and structure-based computational modeling to evaluate their potential impact on protein stability and molecular interactions. RNA analysis confirmed that the CDK12 variant produced the previously reported in-frame one amino acid deletion, whereas the HGS variant activated a cryptic splice acceptor site, resulting in an in-frame deletion affecting a region containing a known ubiquitination site. No aberrant splicing was detected for CEACAM5. Network analyses highlighted convergence of three candidate genes (ERBB3, MAP2K1 and RASA2) on receptor tyrosine kinase signaling and the RAS/MAPK pathway. Structural analyses predicted local perturbations affecting membrane interactions, residue interaction networks, or protein stability for variants in the three previous genes and in USP4, supporting their functional relevance. Integrating RNA-based functional assays with network and structural analyses provides a practical framework for interpreting and prioritizing rare germline VUS identified by WES, supporting the identification of candidate lung cancer susceptibility genes and improving genetic risk assessment.

title: Infrared vibrational fingerprinting for the detection of nucleic acid methylation with structural validation by circular dichroism.
abstract: Nucleic acid methylation is a fundamental epigenetic regulation that influences gene expression and is increasingly explored as a biomarker in cancer biology. However, conventional methods employed for methylation analysis are often labor-intensive, require comprehensive sample preparation, and lack real-time structural sensitivity. Herein, we report an experimentally validated spectroscopic framework for quantitative, label-free detection of methyl (-CH₃) signatures and structural features of nucleic acids using attenuated total reflection Fourier transform infrared (ATR-FTIR) and circular dichroism (CD) spectroscopic techniques. Accordingly, concentration-dependent detection thresholds and spectral resolution limits for DNA and RNA methylation were determined. ATR-FTIR data revealed distinct IR peaks attributed to the asymmetric and symmetric stretching and bending vibrations of the CH₃ groups, and displayed improved spectral separation appearing at intermediate concentrations (~500 ng/μL) of nucleic acids. Comparison of methylated RNA oligonucleotides and cell-derived RNA samples confirmed the robustness of methyl-sensitive spectral markers. CD spectroscopy demonstrated a strong linear correlation between DNA concentration and the ellipticity at 277 nm, consistent with excitonic coupling theory. RNA gave rise to detectable CD signals at lower concentrations (~25 ng/μL), whereas DNA required around 100 ng/μL for reliable structural interpretation, reflecting intrinsic differences between A- and B-form helices. Our study provides (i) experimentally determined lower detection limits, (ii) validated IR vibrational fingerprints of methylation-associated groups, and (iii) a combined spectroscopic analysis suitable for rapid and cost-effective examination of nucleic acid methylation. Thus, the current study lays the groundwork for future applications targeting site-specific modifications such as m6A and 5-methylcytosine in biomolecules.

title: Chrysanthevelides A-D, the Rearranged 5/5/5 Tricyclic Spiro-Guaianolides and 1, 3-Dioxolane-Containing Nor-Guaianolide Dimers from Chrysanthemum vestitum Target PKM2 to Mediate the Anti-Inflammatory Effect.
abstract: Four unprecedented dimeric (1-2) and monomeric (3-4) sesquiterpenoids were isolated from the aerial part of Chrysanthemum vestitum. Chrysanthevelides A-B (1-2) represented the first example of the dimers with a special 1,3-dioxolane nor-guaianolide sesquiterpenoid unit, while chrysanthevelides C-D (3-4) were two pairs of unprecedented 1,10-seco rearranged 5/5/5 tricyclic spiro-guaianolide sesquiterpenoids. The undescribed structures of 1-4, including their absolute configurations, were determined through spectroscopic techniques combined with DP4+ NMR analysis and ECD calculations. Compound 1 displayed an NO production inhibitory effect with an IC50 value of 1.62 ± 0.21 μM. Primarily, western blotting and ELISA combined with the RNA-seq results indicated that 1 suppressed downstream-related inflammatory factors (IL-6 and TNF-α) and proteins (COX-2 and iNOS). Mechanistically, the α-methylene-γ-lactone (αMγL) moiety of 1 covalently binds to Cys423 of PKM2, promoting its tetramerization, which in turn regulates the HIF-1α/STAT3 axis and the glycolytic pathway. This ultimately suppressed the expression of inflammatory mediators, thereby achieving its anti-inflammatory function.

title: Changes of RNA expression in aging periodontal ligament cells.
abstract: Aging is a major risk factor for periodontal disease and is associated with impaired tissue homeostasis and regenerative capacity. The periodontal ligament (PDL) plays a central role in periodontal integrity; however, the molecular mechanisms underlying PDL cell aging remain incompletely understood. In this study, we established an in vitro passage-dependent cellular aging model using human periodontal ligament fibroblasts serially passaged from early to late stages. Transcriptomic changes associated with aging were analyzed using RNA sequencing, followed by principal component analysis, hierarchical clustering, pathway enrichment, and protein-protein interaction network analyses. Global transcriptomic profiling revealed that PDL cell aging follows a non-linear and heterogeneous trajectory rather than a uniform progressive decline. Notably, passage 13 emerged as a distinct transitional stage. Genes with decreasing expression during aging were strongly enriched in biosynthetic and proliferative pathways, including DNA metabolism, rRNA processing, and cell cycle regulation. In contrast, genes with increasing expression showed limited functional convergence and were mainly associated with signaling, immune and cytokine responses, extracellular matrix remodeling, and stress adaptation. Post hoc analysis identified two passage-13-associated gene-expression patterns: 13deep, characterized by residual biosynthetic and proliferative programs, and 13peak, marked by enhanced regulatory, immune, and microenvironment-responsive signaling. This study suggests that the passage 13 may represent a putative transition between biosynthetic decline and regulatory adaptation. Our findings provide a molecular framework for understanding age-related periodontal tissue degeneration and may inform future strategies for early intervention, prevention, and regeneration in periodontal disease associated with aging.

title: Silencing the mir-132/SIRT1 axis suppresses NLRP3 inflammasome activation and myofibroblast differentiation in oral submucous fibrosis.
abstract: Oral submucous fibrosis (OSF) is a chronic oral potentially malignant disorder characterized by progressive extracellular matrix deposition, myofibroblast activation, oxidative stress, and inflammatory signaling. However, the upstream microRNA-mediated mechanisms linking fibrogenesis and NOD-like receptor family pyrin domain-containing protein 3 (NLRP3) inflammasome activation remain unclear. This study investigated the role of the miR-132/sirtuin 1 (SIRT1) axis in OSF-associated fibrotic and inflammatory responses. miR-132 expression was examined in OSF tissues, normal tissues, primary buccal mucosal fibroblasts (BMFs), and fibrotic buccal mucosal fibroblasts (fBMFs) using RNA sequencing and quantitative real-time PCR. Patient-derived fBMFs were transfected with a miR-132 inhibitor or control. Collagen gel contraction, wound healing, intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS), and inflammasome-related protein expression were assessed. TargetScan prediction, luciferase reporter assays, and western blotting were used to evaluate SIRT1 as a miR-132 target. SIRT1 overexpression was further performed to determine its functional effects. miR-132 was significantly expressed in fBMFs and its expression positively correlated with alpha-smooth muscle actin (α-SMA) and COL1A1. MiR-132 inhibition reduced collagen gel contraction, wound closure, ROS generation, and expression of NLRP3, ASC, cleaved caspase-1, cleaved GSDMD, and cleaved IL-1β. SIRT1 was validated as a direct target of miR-132, as miR-132 inhibition increased SIRT1 protein expression and miR-132 mimic suppressed wild-type SIRT1 3'UTR reporter activity. SIRT1 overexpression reduced α-SMA expression, migration, contraction, and inflammasome marker expression in fBMFs. miR-132 promotes OSF-related myofibroblast activation, oxidative stress, and NLRP3 inflammasome signaling partly through SIRT1 suppression. Targeting the miR-132/SIRT1 axis may provide a potential strategy for attenuating OSF progression.

title: Case Report: Coexpression of somatic EGFR, BRCA1, and BRCA2 mutations in metastatic non-small cell lung cancer.
abstract: Treatment of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) has evolved dramatically over the past decade with the advent of widespread genetic testing, immunotherapy, and targeted therapies. Treatments directed against epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) and other driver mutations have reduced toxicity and improved efficacy for selected patients. We present a 59-year-old man with metastatic NSCLC harboring coexisting EGFR, BRCA1, and RNA-binding motif protein 10 (RBM10) mutations and high programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) expression. A BRCA2 mutation was later detected on peripheral blood testing. The patient presented with a debilitating stroke that included dysphagia and hemiparesis. During his course of care, he received osimertinib, after which EGFR and RBM10 variant allele frequencies (VAFs) increased on peripheral blood testing. He also received immunotherapy and olaparib. Despite high response rates reported in the literature, he did not respond to these agents. He had a response to chemotherapy but tolerated it poorly. Ultimately, given the lack of durable response and his inability to tolerate chemotherapy, the patient opted for palliative care. Patients with actionable targets such as EGFR, BRCA1/2, or elevated PD-L1 generally have superior outcomes with targeted and combination therapy compared with patients who lack targetable options. However, coexisting mutations can interact and provide escape mechanisms. The lack of response in our patient is consistent with studies showing reduced efficacy of EGFR-directed therapy in the presence of RBM10 loss-of-function (LOF) alterations. Further research in patients with multiple concurrent mutations is needed to improve treatment options for this group.

title: Amomum tsao-ko volatile oil alleviates renal fibrosis in 5/6 nephrectomy rats through TGF-β1/SMAD3 and PI3K/AKT signaling pathways.
abstract: Renal fibrosis is the main cause of many kidney diseases and a common outcome of many chronic kidney diseases. The dried mature fruit of Amomum tsao-ko is widely used to treat various diseases, including those characterized by diuresis and detumescence. Amomum tsao-ko volatile oil (AO) may be the active ingredient responsible for its main pharmacological action, and its protective effect and mechanism in kidney injury models are unclear. Therefore, based on transcriptomics and animal experiments, this study discusses the mechanism of AO through TGF‑β1/SMAD3 and PI3K/AKT signaling pathways in renal fibrosis of 5/6 nephrectomy rats. Seventy-two healthy SD rats were randomly divided into 6 groups. The rat renal fibrosis model was established by 5/6 nephrectomy. Different doses of AO were given by gavage. After 28 days of continuous administration, the levels of creatinine and urea nitrogen in serum of rats were detected. The total RNA of rat kidney tissue was extracted for transcriptomics determination and analysis showed the expression of differential genes in each group. The core targets related to chronic kidney injury were docked with the main components of the AO. HE, PAS and Masson staining were used to observe the pathological morphology of renal tissue in rats. Western Blot was used to detect the expression of p-PI3K, PI3K, AKT, p-AKT, SMAD3, TGF-β1, MMP-9 and TIMP-1 in renal tissue. Compared with the Sham group, the transcriptome results showed that there were 823 genes with significant differences in expression; the levels of SCr and BUN in the model group were significantly increased. HE, PAS and Masson found that 5/6 Nx could develop interstitial fibrosis. At the same time, a large number of renal tubular epithelial cells were atrophied, deformed and exfoliated, and a large number of inflammatory cells infiltrated in the interstitium. Western Blot results showed that the expression of PI3 K, AKT, TIMP-1, SMAD3, TGF-β1 and other proteins in the 5/6 Nx group increased significantly, and the expression of MMP-9 protein decreased significantly. Compared with the 5/6 Nx group, there were 1,009 genes with significant differences in expression after treatment with AO, and the levels of SCr and BUN decreased. The infiltration of inflammatory cells in renal tissue was improved. The expression of PI3K, AKT, TIMP-1, SMAD3 and TGF-β1 was significantly decreased, and the expression of MMP-9 was significantly increased. AO can further inhibit the phosphorylation level by inhibiting the TGF- β1/SMAD3 and PI3K/AKT signaling pathways in 5/6 Nx rats, thus effectively improving the pathological damage of renal tissue.

title: Nuclear size is genetically controlled and influences cell fate.
abstract: The proportional scaling between nuclear and cell size was first described more than 150 years ago and is among the most conserved features of cellular organization. Yet the mechanisms that establish this scaling and its physiological significance have remained unresolved. Here, we address both questions by combining image-enabled cell sorting with genome-wide CRISPR screening, transcriptomics and functional analyses. We identify more than 180 regulators of the nuclear-to-cell ratio and show that distinct classes of genes independently control nuclear and cell size. RNA metabolism predominantly regulates nuclear size, whereas protein synthesis and degradation primarily regulate cell size. This supports a model in which differences in macromolecular partitioning between the nucleus and cytoplasm contribute to osmotic regulation of nuclear size together with mechanical constraints imposed by chromatin, the cytoskeleton, and the nuclear envelope. Changes in nuclear size cause widespread transcriptional remodeling that is independent of changes in cell size. Cells with smaller nuclei exhibit reduced PRC2-dependent H3K27 trimethylation, activation of developmental gene-expression programmes and repression of cell-cycle genes. Consistent with these changes, mouse embryonic stem cells with smaller nuclei show an increased propensity to exit pluripotency and initiate differentiation in response to retinoic acid. Together, our findings provide a mechanistic framework for nuclear size scaling and establish nuclear size as a physical regulator of gene expression and cell-state transitions, linking cellular architecture to cell fate.

title: LRP2: A proteogenomics pipeline for long-read informed protein isoform analysis and discovery.
abstract: Most human genes produce multiple RNA isoforms, yet it remains unclear which isoforms are translated into stable, functional proteins. Long-read RNA sequencing resolves full-length transcript structures and, when paired with mass spectrometry, can provide empirical evidence of isoform translation. Despite this opportunity, comprehensive workflows integrating isoform discovery, open reading frame prediction, peptide identification, and protein inference remain limited, leaving users to handle these steps piecemeal. Here, we present LRP2, a modular, end-to-end long-read proteogenomics pipeline built in Nextflow. LRP2 scales transcript discovery to hundreds of samples via PacBio's latest Isocall tool, removes technical artifacts with SQANTI QC, generates and classifies predicted proteomes via CPAT and SQANTI Protein, performs multi-group differential expression and usage analysis via edgeR, DRIMSeq, and a long-read adaptation of LeafCutter, and integrates protein-level evidence from DDA and DIA MS data through FragPipe. For cross-dataset comparison of novel isoforms, LRP2 employs deterministic splice-junction, coordinate-based isoform identifiers. Used as an integrated pipeline, LRP2 enables the detection of novel peptides and improves protein isoform inference to confirm protein isoform translation. LRP2 is freely available as a modular Nextflow pipeline at https://github.com/sheynkman-lab/LRP2 (v2.0.0, archived at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22795865). LRP2 supports Docker, Apptainer/Singularity, and Conda environments with GENCODE references. Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.

title: CD147 drives keloid formation by promoting fibroblast proliferation via the CENPF signaling pathway.
abstract: Keloids are benign dermal tumors, and keloid fibroblasts (KFs) play a critical role in their formation through hyperproliferation. However, the mechanism underlying this excessive fibroblast growth in keloids remains elusive. Here, we demonstrate that CD147 is upregulated in KFs and promotes their pathological activities, while its inhibition reverses these abnormalities. RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) analysis revealed that CD147 played an important regulatory role in controlling the cell cycle of KFs, and centromere protein F (CENPF) expression was substantially downregulated following CD147 inhibition. Furthermore, CENPF knockdown attenuated the proliferation-inducing effects of CD147 in KFs, potentially promoting cell apoptosis via the p53 signaling pathway. These findings uncover the CD147-CENPF signaling pathway in keloid pathogenesis, suggesting targeting this pathway as a promising therapeutic strategy.

title: Proteomic Characterization of Prostate Cancer Bone Metastasis Subtypes Defines Progressive Remodeling States of the Bone-Tumor Microenvironment.
abstract: Prostate cancer (PC) bone metastases (PCBM) are a debilitating disease morbidity that primarily affects the axial skeleton. PCBM are predominantly osteosclerotic with mixed osteosclerotic/osteolytic features, including irregular bone deposition, loss of collagen alignment and increased porosity that mimic features of woven bone formed during development and repair. We hypothesize that progression of PCBM is driven by interactions between tumor cells and the bone microenvironment and is associated with changes in the stromal compartment. We performed tandem mass tag mass spectrometry proteomics on lumbar vertebral specimens from 32 cadaveric PCBM specimens and 3 age-matched controls. Unsupervised clustering segregated specimens into three clusters associated with benign, mixed, and osteosclerotic lesion states, characterized by distinct immune-, tumor-, and osteogenic-associated protein signatures. Histological analysis showed tumor infiltration was accompanied by marrow fibrosis and increased collagen III deposition. We identified a marker signature associated with osteosclerotic remodeling and mapped this signature to independent metastatic PC transcriptomic datasets. The proteomics-derived markers reproduced similar molecular groupings at RNA level, and robustly segregated bone PCBMs from soft tissue metastases PC in RNA data. Together, these findings define molecularly distinct states of tumor-driven changes in PCBM that extend beyond histological classification and may inform biomarker development and therapeutic stratification.

title: Restoration of deficient IL-15 signaling enhances innate lymphoid cell immunity in brain metastasis.
abstract: Natural killer (NK) cells and type 1 innate lymphoid cells (ILC1s), collectively known as group 1 innate lymphoid cells (ILCs), are critical mediators of anti-tumor immunity, yet their role in brain metastasis remains poorly defined. Using single-cell RNA sequencing and functional depletion models, we show that group 1 ILCs fail to provide adequate tumor control in breast cancer brain metastasis (BCBM). In contrast to the liver, where diverse, functionally competent group 1 ILC populations facilitate excellent metastatic control, group 1 ILCs in BCBM show limited diversity and profound tissue-specific dysfunction such that their depletion had no effect on tumor burden despite modest parenchymal infiltration. We attribute this group 1 ILC dysfunction to severely restricted IL-15 availability, with IL-15Rα protein detected at 500-fold lower concentration in the brain than in the liver. Local IL-15 complex administration restored group 1 ILC accumulation, cytotoxicity, and tissue residency, significantly reducing brain metastatic burden independent of T cells. Intracranial delivery of IL-15-secreting induced pluripotent stem-cell-derived (iPSC)-NK cells, already in clinical testing for non-small cell lung cancer, significantly reduced tumor burden. Collectively, these findings reveal how tissue-specific differences in cytokine availability shape group 1 ILC population diversity and disease response, establishing localized IL-15 signaling as a compelling strategy to unlock innate immunity against intracranial malignancies. Group 1 ILCs, including NK cells and ILC1s, can be pharmacologically enhanced with IL-15 to improve control of breast cancer brain metastasis.

title: IsoGraph resolves coordinated transcript choice and gene abundance in the aging human brain.
abstract: Relative transcript usage can change without a corresponding change in total gene expression, but resolving coordinated transcript choice across genes while separating it from abundance remains challenging. We present IsoGraph, a gene-centered framework that represents isoform usage and abundance as paired network channels, identifies gene modules, and quantifies their channel-specific contributions. In synthetic benchmarks, IsoGraph preferentially recovered network structure when coordinated transcript usage carried the planted signal, whereas abundance-based representations were more informative in abundance-dominated and RNA-degradation settings. Applied to BrainSEQ and GTEx adult brain transcriptomes, IsoGraph identified age-associated transcript-usage signals that persisted after conditioning on gene abundance and, in a region-dependent manner, after adjustment for estimated cellular composition. Modules were stable across donor subsets, and frozen module axes retained age associations across cohorts even when exact gene partitions differed. IsoGraph module context captured predictive information about held-out differential transcript usage beyond gene-wise evidence and conventional co-expression. Convergent evidence from structural annotation, short-read junction usage, independent long-read sequencing, and within-donor allelic analyses supported constituent transcript events. Disease colocalization further prioritized candidate isoform events at neurological and psychiatric disease loci, including an alternative terminal-exon event at PRDM2 associated with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis. Together, these results establish coordinated transcript usage as a reproducible component of transcriptomic organization and provide a framework for resolving its contribution alongside gene abundance and for tracing network-level signals to candidate transcript events.

title: The RNA helicase KREH2 directly binds the RESC1-RESC2 complex in trypanosomatid mitochondrial RNA editing.
abstract: Trypanosomatids are medically important single-celled eukaryotic protists with exceptional RNA biology. They display highly unusual RNA biogenesis pathways, notably mitochondrial RNA editing, an essential post-transcriptional process transforming cryptic primary transcripts into functional mRNAs. Large multiprotein assemblies coordinate the RNA editing process, in which small guide RNAs (gRNAs) anneal to the pre-mRNAs and serve as templates for uridine insertion or deletion. Kinetoplast RNA Editing Helicases (KREHs) are important components of the RNA editing process that modifies large portions of pre-mRNA via the sequential annealing and dissociation of multiple gRNAs. However, how KREH helicases interact with components of the editing machinery, and which subunits mediate these interactions, remain unresolved. Here, we examined an association between the DEAH/RHA RNA helicase KREH2 and the RESC1-RESC2 protein heterodimer using proximity labeling and co-immunoprecipitation coupled to quantitative mass spectrometry in vivo . We reconstituted a minimal trimeric KREH2 peptide-RESC1-RESC2 complex in vitro and characterized novel direct binding of a KREH2 peptide to RESC1 using cryo-electron microscopy. These results establish a mechanistic link between the RNA helicase KREH2 and the RESC1-RESC2 module at the 5'-end of gRNAs, providing new avenues for studying the orchestration of RNA remodeling in trypanosomatid mitochondrial RNA editing.

title: Establishment and characterization of LNCaP-TR-BoM, a bone metastasis-derived prostate cancer cell line with an intermediate AR-attenuated phenotype.
abstract: Progression of prostate cancer under androgen receptor (AR) pathway-targeted therapy spans a phenotypic spectrum, from tumors that sustain AR pathway output to tumors that become independent of AR signaling. Experimental models that occupy the intermediate portion of this spectrum, in which AR is still expressed but pathway output is reduced, are comparatively scarce. LNCaP cells expressing a triple-modality reporter (LNCaP-TR) were injected into nude mice by the intracardiac route, and a bone lesion that arose in the middle spine of one animal was recovered and propagated as LNCaP-TR-BoM. The subline and its parental line were compared by two-dimensional and three-dimensional culture assays, RNA-seq, qRT-PCR, and immunoblotting. AR pathway output was assessed using KLK3 expression under AR antagonist treatment. Public prostate cancer datasets provided clinical context. A CRISPR-Cas9 EPHA3 -edited derivative was evaluated in aggregation and spheroid assays. Relative to parental LNCaP-TR, LNCaP-TR-BoM formed more numerous and larger cell aggregates in monolayer culture and larger, less circular spheroids in both suspension and Matrigel three-dimensional culture. AR mRNA was modestly reduced and AR protein remained readily detectable, whereas KLK3 mRNA and protein were reduced disproportionately more than those of AR. Residual KLK3 expression remained suppressible by AR inhibitors enzalutamide and darolutamide. Transcriptome-based pseudotime placed LNCaP-TR-BoM between the parental line and the androgen-refractory LNCaP-RF variant. Subsequent differential gene expression (DGE) and pathway enrichment analysis revealed that LNCaP-TR-BoM exhibits transcriptomic rewiring concordant with that of clinical mCRPC, thus evidencing LNCaP-TR-BoM as a potentially clinically relevant model cell line. Finally, EPHA3 showed the largest fold change among the most significant differentially expressed genes in LNCaP-TR-BoM compared with the parental line. Therefore, EPHA3 was explored to demonstrate the utility of the LNCaP-TR-BoM cell line as a discovery system for genes that potentially drive the malignancy of bone-metastatic prostate cancer at the intermediate AR-attenuated progression stage. An EPHA3 -silenced derivative of LNCaP-TR-BoM lacking detectable EPHA3 protein formed smaller aggregates and smaller, more circular spheroids, suggesting EPHA3 may play a role in driving the malignancy of AR-intermediate bone-metastatic prostate cancer. This finding provides support for the potential utility of the LNCaP-TR-BoM cell line as a discovery system for genes relevant to driving AR-intermediate bone-metastatic prostate cancer. LNCaP-TR-BoM is a bone lesion-derived prostate cancer cell line in which AR expression is retained but AR pathway output is attenuated, accompanied by an mCRPC-concordant transcriptomic shift and altered multicellular organization. It provides a paired discovery system for candidate genes such as EPHA3 .

title: Nuclear Factor Kappa-B Inducing Kinase- and Inhibitor of Nuclear Factor Kappa-B Kinase Subunit Beta-Binding Protein Promotes Pathological Cardiac Hypertrophy by Regulating Inhibitor of Nuclear Factor Kappa-B Kinase Subunit Beta-Mediated Nuclear Factor Kappa-B Activation.
abstract: Pathological cardiac hypertrophy is a major risk factor for heart failure. NIBP (NF-κB [nuclear factor kappa-B] inducing kinase- and inhibitor of NF-κB kinase subunit beta-binding protein) is a key regulator of cytokine-induced NF-κB signaling, but its role in cardiac hypertrophy remains unknown. We established transverse aortic constriction-induced cardiac hypertrophy in mice and phenylephrine-induced hypertrophy in neonatal rat ventricular myocytes. Genetic interventions included generation of whole-body Nibp knockout mice via CRISPR-Cas9; creation of cardiomyocyte-specific Nibp knockout mice using adeno-associated virus serotype 9-delivered Cre and single-guide RNAs in Rosa26-LSL-Cas9 mice; and cardiac-specific Nibp overexpression via adeno-associated virus serotype 9delivery. In neonatal rat ventricular myocytes, NIBP was knocked down or overexpressed using adenoviruses. Phenotypes were assessed by echocardiography, histology (wheat germ agglutinin, picrosirius redstaining), and molecular analyses. Mechanisms were investigated via RNA-sequencing, coimmunoprecipitation, and Western blotting for key signaling molecules. NIBP protein was upregulated in hypertrophic hearts and cardiomyocytes. Both Nibp-knockout and cardiomyocyte-specific Nibp knockout attenuated transverse aortic constriction-induced cardiac dysfunction, hypertrophy, and fibrosis, whereas Nibp overexpression exacerbated these pathologies. Consistently, in neonatal rat ventricular myocytes, NIBP knockdown mitigated, while its overexpression aggravated, phenylephrine-induced cardiomyocyte hypertrophy and inflammatory responses. Mechanistically, NIBP directly interacted with IKKβ (inhibitor of NF-κB kinase subunit beta), enhanced its phosphorylation, and drove hyperactivation of the downstream NF-κB pathway. Overexpression of a kinase-dead IKKβ mutant reversed the hypertrophic effects of NIBP. NIBP promotes pathological cardiac hypertrophy by activating the IKKβ/NF-κB axis, identifying it as a potential therapeutic target for cardiac remodeling and heart failure.

title: ATF3 Promotes Solasonine-Triggered Ferroptosis in Glioma Cells by Suppressing Glycolysis.
abstract: Glioma cells are characterized by rapid proliferation, a high degree of invasiveness, and significant heterogeneity. Despite the application of various treatment regimens in recent years, the prognosis for glioma remains poor. The induction of ferroptosis in tumor cells has emerged as a promising therapeutic approach. Solasonine (SS), a steroidal alkaloid derived from plants of the Solanaceae family, has multiple antitumor effects. However, whether it can inhibit glioma growth and its mechanism of action have not been studied. The effects of SS on ferroptosis in glioma cells were analyzed by detecting the levels of ferrous ions, reactive oxygen species, and malondialdehyde. The role of activating transcription factor 3 (ATF3) in SS-induced ferroptosis in glioma cells was analyzed using western blotting, immunofluorescence, and confocal microscopy. An in vivo mouse model of glioma was constructed to further investigate the effects of SS. We found that SS inhibited the proliferation of glioma cells and promoted their ferroptosis. SS treatment increased the intracellular ferrous ion, malondialdehyde, and reactive oxygen species levels. It increased the intracellular hydrogen peroxide level by regulating ATF3 to inhibit glycolysis and suppress the antioxidant system. Increased hydrogen peroxide levels activated nuclear receptor coactivator 4-dependent ferritinophagy and increased intracellular iron levels. Furthermore, SS activated the protein kinase RNA-like endoplasmic reticulum kinase/ATF4 endoplasmic reticulum stress pathway by inhibiting glycolysis and promoted ATF3 expression. This process formed a positive feedback loop. In a murine model, SS significantly inhibited glioma cell growth by inducing ferroptosis. These results indicate that SS promotes glioma cell ferroptosis in vitro and in vivo by inhibiting glycolysis through ATF3.

title: One-carbon metabolism sustains effector T cell function through cell-surface glycosylation.
abstract: Folate is an essential driver of one-carbon metabolism. The cellular consequences of its deprivation in CD8 + T cell and impact on anti-tumor function are unknown. Single cell RNA-seq analysis of primary central nervous system lymphoma (PCNSL) patients' tumor samples revealed exhaustion in T cells with high folate metabolism gene expression signature. Functional genomics, metabolite profiling, and glycomics identified disrupted cell surface glycosylation as a major consequence of folate deprivation in CD8 + T cells. Mechanistically, folate deprivation reduced nucleotide sugar levels, perturbed glycosylation, and triggered the apoptotic unfolded protein response. Overexpressing folate transporters in adoptively transferred CD8 + T cells increased intratumoral T cell numbers and reduced exhaustion. Therefore, our data draw a mechanistic line between one-carbon metabolism, cell-surface glycosylation, and anti-tumor T cell function, and support a hypothesis that increased folate uptake can enhance CD8 + T cell function including ex vivo and in vivo CAR-T cells. Although folate metabolism genes are highly expressed in both proliferating tumor and CD8 + T cells from primary central nervous system lymphoma patients, the T cells are exhausted while the tumor cells thrive Folate is depleted in the TME of MC38-OVA and B16-OVA tumors Folate deprivation impairs function and proliferation of CD8 + T cells Folate is essential for nucleotide sugar metabolism, and its depletion results in perturbation of cell surface glycosylationGenetic engineering to increase folate uptake by T cells increases intratumoral T cell numbers and reduces exhaustion.

title: A long-term organotypic slice culture model of patient high-grade glioma preserving tumor heterogeneity and architecture, and specificity of CAR T cell targeting.
abstract: High grade glioma (HGG), encompassing IDH-wildtype glioblastoma (CNS WHO grade 4), diffuse midline glioma (CNS WHO grade 4), oligodendroglioma (IDH-mutant and 1p/19q-codeleted) CNS WHO grade 3, together with IDH-mutant astrocytoma of CNS grade 3 and grade 4, represents the most lethal group of adult diffuse gliomas. Despite significant efforts, obtaining improvements in patient survival has been limited, in part, by difficulties in comprehensive ex vivo modeling of the complexities of HGG. Although organotypic slice cultures and other platforms have shown promise, existing models often fail to capture the intrinsic cellular heterogeneity, microenvironment, and architecture of HGG, restricting investigations into their fundamental biology as well as design of novel therapeutics. We developed a patient-derived HGG organotypic slice culture (GOSC) platform demonstrating long-term preservation of intrinsic tumor characteristics. Vibratome-sectioned slices were cultured in defined medium under conditions approximating those in situ: reduced oxygen (4%), low glucose (2.5 mM), and no added growth factors. The characteristics of GOSCs after 28 days in culture, including expression of immunotherapy targets, were compared to parental tumors using histological staining, immunofluorescence, multiplexed PhenoCycler (CODEX) imaging, bulk RNA-seq expression profiling, and CAR T cell killing assays. GOSCs preserved the histopathology, cell heterogeneity, tumor microenvironment, and tissue architecture of their parental tumors throughout at least 28 days in culture. Importantly, GOSCs retained parental patterns of immunotherapy target expression, and CAR T cells co-cultured with GOSCs demonstrated target-specific killing consistent with parental tumors. This ex vivo GOSC platform offers long-term preservation of the cellular and structural properties of parental HGG tumors, thereby providing a robust tool for extended preclinical studies, and facilitating development and evaluation of advanced tumor-targeting strategies.

title: RiboFlow v2: a configurable ribosome profiling pipeline reveals measurements sensitive to read-mapping methodology.
abstract: Ribosome profiling experiments capture a snapshot of translation by sequencing ribosome-protected fragments (RPFs). Alignment to a well-curated transcriptome captures most RPF signal, but can miss ribosome activity when expressed exons are absent from the reference. Genome alignment of RPFs expands the detectable sequence space, but can expose ambiguity between homologous loci. Existing workflows often couple reference choice with the handling of ambiguously mapped reads, making it difficult to isolate the effects of either decision on downstream analyses. Here, we developed RiboFlow v2 by adding genome alignment and configurable handling of multimapping reads to the existing transcriptome workflow. Using 24 human ribosome profiling libraries and their matched RNA-seq data, we found that nucleotide-level coverage at matched coding-sequence positions and translation efficiency (TE) were broadly concordant between alignment strategies under stringent alignment filters. Even under these conditions, individual genes showed substantial differences in coverage and TE estimates. These differences included coverage in alternative exons absent from selected transcripts and ambiguous alignments between protein-coding genes and processed pseudogenes. Clustering genes by read-assignment patterns identified groups associated with pseudogene prevalence and highlighted shared exonic sequence among reference transcripts as a source of alignment discrepancies. RiboFlow v2 extends the analysis beyond selected reference transcripts and enables identification of genes whose ribosome coverage and abundance estimates depend on reference composition and how ambiguously mapped reads are handled.

title: mRNA alternative splicing dysregulation in oocytes causes premature ovarian failure.
abstract: Primordial follicle survival determines female reproductive lifespan, yet the post-transcriptional mechanisms governing this process remain incompletely understood. Here, we show that the splicing regulator SRSF2 is required for maintaining the ovarian follicle reserve through the regulation of RNA processing in oocytes. Oocyte-specific ablation of Srsf2 using Gdf9-Cre causes complete female infertility, progressive follicular depletion, and increased follicular apoptosis. Linear amplification of complementary DNA ends and sequencing (LACE-seq) identifies 1609 SRSF2-bound transcripts enriched in RNA-regulatory and cellular homeostasis-related processes. Subsequent RNA-seq analysis reveals broad transcriptomic and alternative-splicing dysregulation after Srsf2 loss, including prominent exon 7 skipping of the oocyte-specific transcription factor Nobox and a marked reduction in full-length NOBOX protein. Supplementation with correctly spliced Nobox mRNA partially rescues follicular developmental defects in vitro, supporting Nobox as a functionally important downstream target rather than the sole mediator of the Srsf2-deficient phenotype. Together, these findings identify SRSF2-dependent RNA processing as an important regulator of oocyte and follicle homeostasis and suggest that disruption of SRSF2-regulated splicing may contribute to ovarian insufficiency.

title: siRNA-Mediated RNF213 Depletion Aggravates Inflammatory Hypoxia-Induced Endothelial Dysfunction and Alters Endothelial-Smooth-Muscle Communication in an In Vitro Model Relevant to Moyamoya Disease.
abstract: Moyamoya disease is a progressive cerebrovascular disorder associated with variants in ring finger protein 213 (RNF213), endothelial dysfunction and pathological arterial remodelling. However, the relationship between reduced RNF213 abundance, inflammatory hypoxia and endothelial-smooth-muscle communication remains incompletely understood. This study investigated the effects of small interfering RNA (siRNA)-mediated RNF213 depletion in primary human brain microvascular endothelial cells exposed to combined hypoxia, tumour necrosis factor alpha (TNF-α) and interferon gamma (IFN-γ). Endothelial viability, proliferation, apoptosis, migration, angiogenic network formation and barrier integrity were evaluated. Conditioned-medium and indirect co-culture systems were subsequently used to examine responses in primary human brain vascular smooth muscle cells. Combined RNF213 depletion and inflammatory hypoxia reduced endothelial viability and proliferation, increased apoptosis, impaired migration and network formation, and compromised barrier integrity. Barrier impairment was demonstrated by decreased transendothelial electrical resistance, increased dextran permeability and disruption of vascular endothelial cadherin (VE-cadherin), zonula occludens-1 (ZO-1), claudin-5 and occludin. RNF213 depletion also enhanced endothelial inflammatory activation. Conditioned medium from RNF213-depleted inflammatory-hypoxic endothelial cells was associated with increased smooth-muscle-cell proliferation, migration and colony formation. These responses were accompanied by reduced contractile-marker expression and increased secreted phosphoprotein 1 (SPP1), Krüppel-like factor 4 (KLF4), fibronectin 1 (FN1) and matrix metalloproteinase 9 (MMP9), consistent with transition toward a synthetic, matrix-remodelling phenotype. The responsible endothelial-derived mediator or combination of mediators was not identified. Selected findings were reproduced using indirect co-culture and an independent siRNA targeting a different RNF213 sequence. These findings support an association between siRNA-mediated RNF213 depletion, endothelial stress susceptibility and altered endothelial-smooth-muscle communication in an in-vitro model relevant to Moyamoya disease. RNF213 re-expression or orthogonal genetic validation will be required to establish RNF213-specific causality.Clinical Trial Number None.

title: RNA-Based Biological Age Clocks Track Chronological Age in Skeletal Muscle but Show Limited Discrimination of Sarcopenia.
abstract: Transcriptomic biological age clocks may track age-related transcriptional variation in skeletal muscle, but it remains unclear whether they detect sarcopenia-related molecular variation beyond chronological age. This multicohort study benchmarked directly implementable RNA-based age models in public human skeletal muscle RNA-seq datasets. GSE164471 was used as a healthy-aging reference, GSE111006/GSE111010 as a pooled discovery benchmark, GSE167186 as external validation, and GSE174106 as biological validation using appendicular lean mass trajectories. RNAAgeCalc skeletal muscle and across-tissue models were implemented for age estimation and sarcopenia discrimination. Gene coverage was used only as a preliminary technical-compatibility assessment, after which the published SkeletAge model was directly applied to GSE111006 and GSE111010 for independent chronological-age prediction and sarcopenia-discrimination analyses; GSE164471, which contributed to SkeletAge model development, was used only for an in-sample implementation check. Both RNAAgeCalc models showed high gene coverage. In GSE164471, the skeletal muscle model showed stronger chronological-age tracking than the across-tissue model (r = 0.604 vs. 0.266; MAE 15.2 vs. 16.7 years), but retained substantial absolute prediction error and positive mean bias (+ 10.4 years), indicating that stronger correlation did not imply adequate calibration. In the discovery benchmark, between-group differences in chronological age, transcriptomic age, and age-acceleration residuals were not statistically significant, with small-to-moderate standardized effect estimates and confidence intervals spanning zero. Logistic discrimination was influenced mainly by cohort origin, while transcriptomic aging measures provided limited independent discrimination. External validation showed broad age-group structure with substantial overlap between old healthy and sarcopenic participants, and no differences were detected across appendicular lean mass trajectories. Current RNAAgeCalc implementations therefore appear to track chronological-age-related transcriptomic structure more effectively than sarcopenia-related variation, although smaller disease-related effects cannot be excluded, and these models should not currently be considered standalone sarcopenia biomarkers.

title: The pH-PI3K/AKT/mTORC1 axis in the survival of stem cells from the apical papilla: A critical target for rescue by microenvironment-engineered hydrogels in pulp regeneration.
abstract: The pH within infected root canals fluctuates dynamically under pathological conditions, yet its impact on stem cells from the apical papilla (SCAPs) in dental pulp regeneration remains unclear. This study investigated how potential of hydrogen (pH) variations govern SCAPs survival and the associated signaling to identify therapeutic targets for enhancing tissue regeneration. SCAPs were cultured at pH 5.4-10.4. Proliferation and apoptosis were assessed using cell counting kit-8 (CCK-8) assays, real-time live-cell analysis, and flow cytometry. RNA-sequencing (RNA-seq) identified differentially expressed genes, which were validated through reverse transcription-quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR), Western blotting, and mechanistic target of rapamycin (mTOR) inhibition. The buffering capacity of RATEA16 hydrogel was also evaluated. Proliferative capacity peaked at pH 7.4, whereas pH 5.4 significantly inhibited proliferation without inducing apoptosis. The phosphoinositide 3-kinase (PI3K)/protein kinase B (AKT)/mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 1 (mTORC1) signaling axis was identified as the key regulatory node. pH 5.4 suppressed the phosphorylation of PI3K, eukaryotic translation initiation factor 4E-binding protein 1 (4EBP1), and ribosomal protein S6 kinase beta-1 (S6K1). Acid-induced inhibition was reversible upon neutralization. The biocompatible RATEA16 hydrogel maintained microenvironmental neutrality and rescued SCAPs proliferation at pH 5.4. Acidic environments inhibited SCAPs proliferation via PI3K/AKT/mTORC1 downregulation. RATEA16 hydrogel restored proliferation through extracellular pH modulation, representing a promising strategy to enhance dental pulp regeneration.

title: Exploring the molecular mechanism of cellular senescence induced by Picrasma quassioides in HepG2 based on RNA sequencing.
abstract: This study investigates the impact of Picrasma quassioides (PQ) on senescence and proliferation in the human hepatoma cell line HepG2, alongside its potential molecular mechanisms, using RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) in conjunction with in vitro experiments. The study aims to provide a novel theoretical foundation for PQ-based hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) treatments. The analysis of chemical components in PQ-containing serum was conducted using UHPLC-Q-Orbitrap HRMS. To assess cell viability, proliferation, and senescence, CCK-8 assays, EdU staining assays, and SA-β-Gal staining assays were performed. Additionally, core differential genes were screened through transcriptome sequencing and network pharmacology. The molecular mechanisms underlying PQ-induced senescence in HepG2 cells were thoroughly elucidated via functional enrichment analysis, construction of protein-protein interaction networks, and molecular docking techniques. Using UHPLC-Q-Orbitrap HRMS technology, 33 chemical components were identified in PQ. The CCK8 assay demonstrated that PQ exhibited a cytotoxic effect on HepG2 cells, while EdU and SA-β-Gal assays confirmed that PQ could induce cellular senescence and inhibit excessive proliferation. RNA sequencing, in conjunction with network pharmacology, identified 146 key genes, and enrichment analysis revealed that these genes were significantly enriched in the MAPK and PI3K-Akt pathways. Among these, five core targets were identified: MMP2, TGFB1, CXCL8, JUN, and FOS. Molecular docking studies suggested that these core genes could interact with PQ-like compounds. PQ exerts anti-cancer effects on HCC by inducing cellular senescence, potentially through the MAPK and PI3K-Akt signaling pathways. MMP2, TGFB1, CXCL8, JUN, and FOS may represent key targets of PQ-induced senescence.

title: Single nucleus RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics reveal unique functionalities of gray matter versus white matter oligodendrocytes in aging and Alzheimer's Disease.
abstract: Oligodendrocyte (OL) dysfunction and white-matter (WM) vulnerability are increasingly recognized as important aspects of aging and Alzheimer's Disease (AD), yet human WM-focused, cellular-resolution transcriptomic data remain limited. Here, we profiled prefrontal WM from 48 brain donors spanning young adulthood and late-life with low versus high AD Neuropathologic Change (ADNC) using single-nucleus RNA sequencing followed by spatial transcriptomics (CosMx) in a subset of matched donors. We integrated aged WM OLs with a reference dorsolateral prefrontal cortex grey-matter (GM) OL dataset (SEA-AD) to define region- and pathology-associated OL programs. Across modalities, GM OLs exhibited a robust synapse/neurotransmitter-associated transcriptional signature relative to WM OLs, whereas this program was reduced with aging and attenuated in high ADNC GM. In contrast, WM OLs showed stronger immune-associated programs with aging and further enhancement in high ADNC, including cytokine/chemokine signaling and antigen presentation-related pathways. High ADNC WM OLs also displayed amplified proteostasis and stress-adaptation signatures, including selective upregulation of chaperone/heat shock genes and ferritin subunits, consistent with increased protein-folding demand and altered iron handling. To resolve OL state organization beyond static differential expression, we annotated OL sub-states using marker panels and inferred pseudotime-guided directional state-to-state flows within each tissue/condition stratum. This analysis identified a conserved newly formed differentiating (NFOL)/differentiating → lipid remodeling (APOE/ABCA1/LPL+) → Stress/ISR-reactive architecture, with a pronounced expansion of the Stress/ISR-reactive compartment and altered transition-associated pathway enrichment in high ADNC WM. Together, these data define WM-specific OL programs linked to aging and ADNC and nominate a stress/immune-enriched OL state landscape consistent with a putative senescence-like phenotype in diseased WM.

title: Promoter architecture and developmental-expression divergence in the Daphnia pulex complex.
abstract: Changes in gene regulation are central to developmental evolution, yet how transcription-initiation architecture contributes to developmental expression divergence remains poorly understood. Here, we integrated chromosome-level genome assemblies, developmental RNA-seq, and STRIPE-seq-based transcription start site (TSS) profiling to examine regulatory divergence between two lineages of the Daphnia pulex complex, KAP4 and CON21, across embryonic, juvenile, and adult stages. The two lineages shared a broadly conserved developmental transcriptional program, but KAP4 consistently expressed more protein-coding genes and long non-coding RNAs than CON21. Genes with stage-specific expression were weakly expressed and showed elevated nucleotide diversity and sequence divergence relative to persistently expressed genes, consistent with relaxed purifying selection. Comparative transcriptomic analyses revealed strong stage-dependent expression divergence between the two lineages: the greatest similarity occurred during late embryonic to early juvenile development rather than mid-embryogenesis, providing limited support for a canonical developmental hourglass pattern. STRIPE-seq uncovered a conserved two-peak TSS organization upstream of annotated translation-start sites, but the relative use of distal and proximal initiation regions differed between lineages. Motif analyses further indicated that these initiation regions are associated with distinct cis-regulatory sequence environments. Promoter shape was closely linked to transcriptional output, with broad promoters showing the highest expression, peaked promoters the lowest, and intermediate promoters occupying an intermediate state. Together, these findings suggest that developmental regulatory divergence in the D. pulex complex is shaped by fine-scale remodeling of TSS usage and promoter architecture.

title: TRPV1-cardiac afferent ablation after completed myocardial infarction prevents arrhythmogenic remodeling.
abstract: Therapies to prevent ventricular arrhythmias after completed myocardial infarction (MI) remain limited. Although TRPV1 afferent ablation at acute MI improves cardiac remodeling, the effect of delayed subacute targeting remains unknown. We investigated whether ablating cardiac TRPV1 afferents during the subacute post-MI window mitigates structural, electrophysiological, and neuro-cardiac axis remodeling to suppress ventricular arrhythmias. Yorkshire pigs underwent sham surgery or anterior MI creation. Two weeks post-MI, animals were randomized to percutaneous epicardial resiniferatoxin (RTX, for cardiac-selective TRPV1 afferent depletion) or vehicle administration. Four weeks later, terminal studies assessed the effects of RTX on cardiac structure and function, ventricular arrhythmogenesis, and neuro-cardiac axis remodeling using in vivo electrophysiologic mapping, real-time neurotransmitter sensing, immunohistochemistry, and transcriptomic profiling.
