Cardiac TRPV1 afferent depletion was confirmed by blunted responses to TRPV1 agonists. RTX-treated animals exhibited improved left ventricular function, reduced end-diastolic diameter, and suppressed ventricular tachycardia/fibrillation (VT/VF) inducibility. Endocardial electroanatomic mapping revealed improved VT/VF electrophysiologic correlates in RTX-treated animals, including fewer deceleration zones and late potentials. Epicardial multielectrode mapping demonstrated reduced electrophysiologic heterogeneity in the scar border zone. Real-time release of adrenergic neurotransmitters (noradrenaline and neuropeptide Y) was normalized during sympathoexcitation in RTX-treated animals. Histologically, RTX treatment attenuated scar border zone myocardial fibrosis and sympathetic nerve sprouting, while suppressing T cell infiltration in cardiac sensory ganglia. Bulk RNA-sequencing of stellate ganglia revealed downregulation of adrenergic genes. Cardiac TRPV1 afferent ablation post-completed MI alters disease trajectory by mitigating structural, functional, and neuro-cardiac axis remodeling. Targeting cardiac TRPV1 afferents represents a promising subacute post-MI therapeutic strategy. Therapies to prevent ventricular arrhythmias following completed myocardial infarction (MI) remain limited, and the impact of targeting cardiac TRPV1 afferents during the subacute phase is unknown. We evaluated whether epicardial resiniferatoxin (RTX) administration two weeks post-MI in swine mitigates structural, electrophysiological, and neuro-cardiac remodeling to suppress ventricular arrhythmogenesis. Four weeks post-treatment, RTX-treated animals exhibited improved left ventricular function, reduced chamber dilation, and suppressed ventricular tachycardia/fibrillation (VT/VF) inducibility compared with controls. Electroanatomic and multielectrode mapping revealed fewer deceleration zones, smaller late potential areas, and reduced repolarization heterogeneity in the scar border zone. Real-time neurotransmitter sensing demonstrated normalized adrenergic release during sympathoexcitation. Histological and transcriptomic profiling showed that RTX attenuated border-zone fibrosis, decreased sympathetic nerve sprouting, suppressed sensory ganglion T-cell infiltration, and downregulated stellate ganglion adrenergic gene expression. Cardiac TRPV1 afferent ablation during the subacute post-MI window alters disease trajectory by mitigating structural and autonomic remodeling, representing a promising disease-modifying therapeutic strategy.

title: Morpholino-mediated splice switching of NELFE suppresses hepatocellular carcinoma cell phenotypes in vitro and in vivo.
abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is among the deadliest cancers worldwide, with rising incidence and few targeted therapies, driving high rates of recurrence and poor survival. Negative elongation factor E (NELFE), an RNA-binding subunit of the NELF complex, acts oncogenically when overexpressed and is associated with worse prognosis in HCC, yet no therapies target it. Here, we identify a rare germline intronic variant in the NELFE locus, NM_002904.6:c.943-110C>T (rs79208225) that promotes skipping of NELFE exon 10 and identifies patients with a trend toward longer recurrence-free survival and lower NELFE expression in their tumors. Mechanistically, the variant reduces U2AF2 occupancy at intron 9, likely through an indirect effect on splice-site recognition rather than direct disruption of U2AF2 binding. Recognizing exon 10 as a targetable splice event, we designed morpholino (MO) antisense oligonucleotides against its splice junctions that phenocopied the variant, lowering NELFE protein expression and impairing malignant phenotypes across HCC cell lines spanning diverse etiologies and NELFE expression levels. Delivered by ultrasound-targeted microbubble destruction (UTMD) in orthotopic liver tumors, NELFE MOs significantly reduced tumor burden and extended survival. These findings establish a naturally occurring splicing event as the basis for a localized, splice-switching therapeutic strategy for HCC.

title: Integrated single-cell and proteomic profiling of pancreatic neoplasia identifies tissue markers that outperform established diagnostic markers in distinguishing cancer from precursor lesions.
abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) arises within an extensively remodeled microenvironment, yet tissue markers that distinguish invasive carcinoma from precursor lesions remain limited. Integrating four single-cell RNA-sequencing atlases comprising 324,662 cells from 26 patients, we identified cancer-associated fibroblast expansion, accumulation of C1QA+ immunoregulatory macrophages, and depletion of a dendritic-cell compartment expressing plasmacytoid markers. Fibroblasts were enriched for extracellular-matrix and PI3K-AKT programs and macrophages for an antigen-presentation program. We then examined the protein-level correlates of these populations in a tissue proteomic reference framework of 356 samples spanning non-diseased pancreas, normal-adjacent tissue, low- and high-grade intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasms (IPMNs), IPMN-associated invasive carcinoma, and PDAC, prioritizing proteins that changed monotonically across the six histopathologic reference groups or marked tumor-enriched cell types. Despite depletion of plasmacytoid dendritic cells, the principal source of type I interferon, the interferon-stimulated protein ISG15, expressed by both fibroblasts and macrophages, increased monotonically toward PDAC. In exploratory cross-validated benchmarking of PDAC versus low- and high-grade IPMN, excluding IPMN-associated invasive carcinoma (145 versus 56 samples), CATB+EPIPL achieved an AUC of 0.98, with a sensitivity of 92% at an achieved specificity of 92%, exceeding protein-abundance models of diagnostic IHC-associated markers (S100P+IMP3+maspin+MSLN, 0.79) and refitted published IPMN-progression combinations (≤0.91). Against non-diseased pancreas, candidate and comparator panels performed similarly (AUC 0.99-1.00). These biologically informed tissue protein panels warrant independent validation, including immunohistochemical evaluation of EUS-guided fine-needle biopsy specimens and measurement in blood.

title: The dark transcriptome mouse organogenesis cell atlas.
abstract: Single-cell atlases have transformed our understanding of mammalian tissue biology, yet the diverse noncoding "dark transcriptome" remains largely uncharted. Here, we present the Dark Transcriptome Mouse Organogenesis Cell Atlas (DT-MOCA), comprising 276,455 cells across embryonic days 11 to 18 and jointly capturing protein-coding transcripts and five major classes of noncoding RNAs through single-nucleus total RNA sequencing, establishing the first comprehensive catalog of noncoding RNAs across major cell types and developmental lineages. We found that long noncoding RNA and microRNA profiles distinguished major cell types and developmental lineages with resolution comparable to messenger RNA, whereas transfer RNA, small nuclear RNA, and small nucleolar RNA programs were less cell type-discriminative and more broadly shared. We further resolve noncoding RNA expression patterns as lineage-specific, temporally modulated, or coordinately regulated by cell identity and developmental stage. We observed that temporally regulated long noncoding RNAs were evolutionarily younger than those associated with cell identity. We further generate a catalog of the change of noncoding RNAs cross all 11 major developmental trajectories. It revealed lineage-specific coordination between transfer RNA supply and codon demand during musculoskeletal organogenesis as well as dynamic microRNA and small nucleolar RNA programs during the central nervous system development. We observed microRNAs converge on regulators of proliferation and gliogenesis and shared induction of Snord116 defining a developmental window relevant to Prader-Willi syndrome. Together, this atlas provides a comprehensive catalog of the developmental dark transcriptome and reveals how noncoding RNA programs are organized across cell identity, developmental time, and lineage progression.

title: Computational identification of candidate human long noncoding RNAs associated with PBMC responses to Candida auris and its cell wall components.
abstract: Candida auris is an emerging multidrug-resistant fungal pathogen. However, little is known about the role of long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs) in the human immune response to this fungus. This study aimed to identify and prioritize novel lncRNAs associated with the response of human peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) to C. auris and its cell wall components. We reanalyzed RNA-sequencing data from peripheral blood mononuclear cells obtained from three healthy donors. The cells were exposed to live C. auris , purified mannan, purified β-glucan, or RPMI control for 4 h or 24 h. We identified 607 putative novel polyadenylated lncRNA loci that were absent from GENCODE Release 48. Of the 449 novel loci tested for differential expression, 102 responded to at least one stimulus. Novel-lncRNA responses were limited at 4 h but increased markedly at 24 h. At 24 h, 78 novel lncRNAs responded to live C. auris , 34 to mannan, and 11 to β-glucan. Many of these responses are specific to a particular stimulus. Among the 102 responsive lncRNAs, 94 were significantly coexpressed with protein-coding genes. The coding genes of the most highly connected lncRNAs were associated with innate immunity, defense responses, lysosomal functions, and signaling pathways. Temporal analysis revealed 19 novel lncRNAs whose responses changed between 4 and 24 h. Fourteen novel lncRNAs were also differentially expressed and were selected for further analysis. Combining temporal response, coexpression, and genomic proximity identified 4 candidate cis-associated pairs: MSTRG.32011-TLR2, MSTRG.5763-DUSP5, MSTRG.25627-HCK, and MSTRG.18159-ITGB3. These findings reveal a predominantly late and stimulus-specific novel-lncRNA response to C. auris and provide prioritized candidates for experimental validation.

title: Macrophage-Derived Glycoprotein Nonmetastatic Melanoma Protein B Attenuates Cardiac Dysfunction by Promoting Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor-Independent Angiogenesis.
abstract: Pressure overload-induced heart failure involves maladaptive cardiac remodeling and inadequate angiogenesis. The limitations of VEGF (vascular endothelial growth factor)-based therapies underscore the need to identify alternative angiogenic pathways. GPNMB (glycoprotein nonmetastatic melanoma protein B) is a macrophage-secreted protein implicated in tissue repair, but its role in pressure overload-induced cardiac remodeling and its potential to modulate angiogenesis remain unknown. Myeloid-specific Gpnmb knockout and control mice were subjected to transverse aortic constriction. Cardiac function, remodeling, and capillary density were assessed. Single-cell RNA sequencing was performed to identify transcriptomic changes. In vitro, human endothelial cells were treated with recombinant GPNMB to assess proliferation, migration, and tube formation, and to dissect the underlying signaling pathways. The therapeutic potential of Gpnmb overexpression was evaluated using AAV9 vectors. Myeloid Gpnmb deletion exacerbated transverse aortic constriction-induced cardiac dysfunction, hypertrophy, fibrosis, and capillary rarefaction. Single-cell sequencing revealed a reduced capillary endothelial cell population and pathway enrichment indicative of endothelial dysfunction and metabolic reprogramming in myeloid-specific Gpnmb knockout hearts. Mechanistically, GPNMB directly promoted endothelial cell proliferation, migration, and tube formation by activating the mTOR (mechanistic target of rapamycin) pathway in a CD44-dependent manner, independently of VEGF signaling. Cardiac-specific Gpnmb overexpression rescued angiogenesis, improved cardiac function, and attenuated pathological remodeling after transverse aortic constriction. Macrophage-derived GPNMB is a critical regulator of cardiac adaptation to pressure overload. It promotes a VEGF-independent angiogenic program probably via the CD44/mTOR axis, as supported by in vitro mechanistic studies. GPNMB represents a promising therapeutic target for heart failure characterized by microvascular rarefaction.

title: The Role of METTL3-Mediated m6A Methylation in Hepatocellular Carcinoma Progression and Treatment.
abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a major cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide. Emerging evidence has established N6-methyladenosine (m6A) RNA methylation as a key epitranscriptomic mechanism underlying hepatocarcinogenesis. Methyltransferase-like 3 (METTL3), the catalytic core of the m6A methyltransferase complex (MTC), forms a heterodimer with METTL14 and cooperates with auxiliary components of the MTC to deposit m6A modifications that modulate mRNA stability, splicing, nuclear export, and translation. In this review, we comprehensively summarize the current understanding of METTL3 biology in HCC, focusing on its structure, assembly within the MTC, regulation of coding and non-coding RNAs, and its roles in driving key oncogenic signaling cascades, such as JAK/STAT3, PI3K/AKT/mTOR, Wnt/β-catenin, Hippo/YAP, Notch, Hedgehog, and epithelial-mesenchymal transition. In addition, we discussed how METTL3 remodels the tumor immune microenvironment (TIME) by regulating immune responses and metabolic pathways promoting immune evasion and therapy resistance. Therapeutic strategies targeting METTL3-including small-molecule inhibitors, CRISPR-Cas9 approaches, combination immunotherapy, and tumor-selective delivery systems-are discussed together with the challenges that continue to limit clinical translation. Collectively, these findings position METTL3 as a central epitranscriptomic regulator of HCC progression; however, further mechanistic and clinical validation remains necessary to establish its utility as a therapeutic target and prognostic biomarker.

title: Ziyin Huatan Recipe Inhibits Lymph Node Metastasis in Gastric Cancer via Downregulating PLAG1-Mediated VEGF-C/VEGFR-3 Signaling.
abstract: To investigate the anti-lymphangiogenic and anti-metastatic effects of Ziyin Huatan Recipe (ZYHT) on gastric cancer (GC), and to elucidate the underlying molecular mechanisms, with a particular focus on the pleomorphic adenoma gene 1 (PLAG1)/vascular endothe lial growth factor C (VEGF-C)/vascular endothe lial growth factor receptor 3 (VEGFR-3) signaling axis. ZYHT was quality-controlled by UHPLC-Q-TOF-MS, and 3 doses (50, 100, 200 µg/mL) were selected. Human GC MGC-803 and HLECs were used. Lymphangiogenesis, migration, and permeability were evaluated by tube formation, Transwell, and FITC-dextran permeability assays, respectively. Secreted VEGF-C was measured by ELISA. In vivo, a popliteal lymph node metastasis model was established by footpad injection of MGC-803 cells in nude mice, followed by intragastric administration of ZYHT (940, 1,880, 3,760 mg•kg-1•d-1) for 3 weeks. RNA-seq and bioinformatics were performed to identify differential expressed genes (DEGs) and pathways. PLAG1-modified cells were established by lentiviral transduction. Proliferation and VEGF-C/VEGFR-3 signaling related protein expression were assessed via CCK-8, colony formation, and Western blot. PLAG1-driven VEGF-C transcription was verified by dual-luciferase assay. ZYHT effectively inhibits GC lymph node metastasis both in vitro and in vivo. Additionally, ZYHT could suppress the activity of VEGF-C/VEGFR-3. Transcriptomic analysis revealed 7,739 DEGs following ZYHT treatment. Furthermore, PLAG1 was identified as a critical transcription factor involved in lymph node metastasis in GC through its regulation of VEGF-C/VEGFR-3 pathway. ZYHT is an effective compound for inhibiting lymph node metastasis in GC via downregulation of PLAG1-mediated VEGF-C/VEGFR-3 signaling. Additionally, PLAG1 may serve as a significant biomarker during the process of GC metastasis through regulating VEGF-C/VEGFR-3 pathway.

title: NAE1-Dependent Protein Neddylation Preserves Endothelial Identity and Vascular Integrity.
abstract: Endothelial dysfunction is a central driver of cardiovascular and inflammatory diseases, yet the post-translational mechanisms that preserve endothelial homeostasis remain incompletely understood. Protein neddylation, the covalent conjugation of a ubiquitin-like modifier, regulates diverse cellular processes, yet its physiological role in the vascular endothelium remains unknown. This study investigated whether protein neddylation is required to preserve endothelial identity and vascular homeostasis. We generated tamoxifen-inducible endothelial-specific Nae1 knockout mice to inhibit neddylation and combined bulk RNA sequencing, single-cell and single-nucleus transcriptomics, quantitative proteomics, biochemical analyses, and gain- and loss-of-function approaches to define the role of endothelial neddylation in vascular homeostasis and inflammatory injury. Endothelial-specific Nae1 deletion caused rapid mortality associated with vascular leakage, platelet accumulation, inflammation, and multi-organ injury. Multi-omics analyses demonstrated profound loss of endothelial identity, characterized by suppression of core endothelial programs and activation of inflammatory, procoagulant, and pyroptotic pathways. Single-cell analyses revealed progressive endothelial dysfunction culminating in depletion of the endothelial population and remodeling of the vascular niche. Mechanistically, endothelial neddylation deficiency activated gasdermin D (GSDMD)- and gasdermin E (GSDME)-dependent pyroptosis, whereas dual inhibition of GSDMD and GSDME markedly attenuated inflammatory transcriptomic remodeling, vascular injury, hepatocyte death, immune cell infiltration, and platelet accumulation. Translational analyses demonstrated reduced endothelial neddylation in experimental endotoxemia and decreased expression of neddylation pathway components in human atherosclerosis and COVID-19 datasets. Conversely, restoration of endothelial neddylation partially reversed inflammatory endothelial transcriptomic reprogramming in vivo. NAE1-dependent protein neddylation is an essential regulator of endothelial identity and vascular integrity. Loss of endothelial neddylation promotes gasdermin-dependent pyroptosis and thrombo-inflammatory vascular injury, whereas restoration of the neddylation pathway mitigates inflammatory endothelial dysfunction. These findings identify endothelial neddylation as a fundamental mechanism maintaining vascular homeostasis and a potential therapeutic target for cardiovascular and inflammatory diseases. What Is New?Endothelial-specific deletion of NAE1, the enzyme that initiates protein neddylation, causes rapid mortality in mice from multi-organ tissue damage, cell death, and inflammation.Neddylation loss activates the pyroptosis executioners GSDMD and GSDME, and silencing GSDMD and GSDME together reverses the transcriptomic and tissue-level damage caused by neddylation deficiency.The endothelial neddylation pathway is significantly downregulated in human clinical conditions, including atherosclerosis and COVID-19, as well as in experimental models of systemic inflammation.What Are the Clinical Implications?Reduced neddylation in atherosclerotic human arteries suggests this pathway could serve as a biomarker or intervention point for endothelial dysfunction in cardiovascular disease.GSDMD and GSDME represent potential therapeutic targets for protecting endothelial integrity in vascular and inflammatory diseases, including endotoxemia.Because neddylation inhibitors such as MLN4924 (pevonedistat) are already in clinical use for cancer, these findings suggest a mechanism behind their reported vascular and hepatic toxicity that warrants monitoring.

title: Integrated Transcriptomic and Network Pharmacology Identifies IRF1, PTGS2, TNF, and IFNG as Candidate Targets of Cortex Dictamni in Atopic Dermatitis.
abstract: Cortex Dictamni has been used in traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) for inflammatory skin disorders, but its potential molecular targets in atopic dermatitis (AD) remain incompletely characterized. Active compounds and predicted targets of Cortex Dictamni were retrieved from the Traditional Chinese Medicine Systems Pharmacology Database and Analysis Platform and integrated with bulk-transcriptomic differential-expression data and single-cell RNA-sequencing data. Protein-protein interaction, functional-enrichment, gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA), and single-sample GSEA (ssGSEA)-based immune-cell and pathway analyses were performed with Benjamini-Hochberg correction for multiple testing. Molecular docking was used to predict luteolin-IFNG and β-sitosterol-PTGS2 binding poses, and candidate-gene expression was assessed in TNF-α/IFN-γ-stimulated HaCaT keratinocytes treated with low concentrations of purified dictamnine. Eighteen active components yielded 170 predicted targets; 88 overlapped with AD-related genes, and 43 of these were differentially expressed. Intersecting 366 cell-type-specific differentially expressed genes with 42 targets identified IRF1, PTGS2, TNF, and IFNG. IRF1, PTGS2, and TNF were upregulated in specific immune-cell populations, whereas IFNG was downregulated in natural killer cells. Ribosome-pathway enrichment was observed across five immune-cell types. After Benjamini-Hochberg correction, immune-signature correlations were gene-specific and bidirectional, whereas Hallmark-pathway correlations were nonsignificant. Docking predicted possible binding poses for luteolin-IFNG and β-sitosterol-PTGS2. In TNF-α/IFN-γ-stimulated HaCaT cells, 6.25 and 12.5 µM dictamnine reduced all four mRNAs, whereas 12.5 µM dictamnine alone had no significant effect. Collectively, IRF1, PTGS2, TNF, and IFNG were nominated as potential Cortex Dictamni-associated targets in AD, and low-dose purified dictamnine provided preliminary mRNA-level support. These findings do not establish crude-herb efficacy or direct target-compound interactions and require protein-level, mechanistic, in vivo, and clinical validation.

title: Comparative Transcriptomic Signatures of Keloids and Hypertrophic Scars: A Genetic Association Pilot Study.
abstract: Keloids and hypertrophic scars are fibroproliferative skin disorders with overlapping clinical features but distinct biological behaviors, posing major therapeutic challenges in plastic and reconstructive surgery. Understanding their molecular mechanisms is critical for developing targeted interventions. A comparative study of transcriptomic profiles of keloid (n = 3) and hypertrophic scar (n = 3) lesions from female patients (thoracic region, no comorbidities). RNA-seq was performed, and differential gene expression was analyzed using DESeq2. Functional enrichment analyses were conducted via Gene Ontology and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes, stratifying upregulated and downregulated genes. Keloids exhibited upregulation of genes involved in ribosome biogenesis, RNA splicing, chromosomal organization, and cell cycle progression (eg, USP39, CEP85, RNF180, VHL), reflecting a sustained anabolic and proliferative state. In contrast, hypertrophic scars were enriched in immune and metabolic pathways, with higher expression of ICAM1, MRC1/CD206, PDE2A, TMEM120A, and TMEM135, suggesting modulation by inflammatory cytokines (interleukin-6, transforming growth factor beta) and M2 macrophage polarization. Integrated Gene Ontology and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes analyses highlighted central pathways including transforming growth factor beta, nuclear factor κB, advanced glycation end products-receptor for advanced glycation end products, and cAMP response element-binding protein, with polycomb repressive complex activation identified as a shared yet differentially regulated epigenetic axis. This study revealed distinct molecular signatures in keloid and hypertrophic scars, elucidating divergent mechanisms of fibroblast proliferation, inflammation, and tissue remodeling. These findings provide a mechanistic framework for translational strategies in plastic surgery, including precision-targeted therapies, drug repurposing, and gene-based interventions, advancing management of pathological skin fibrosis and improving surgical outcomes.

title: LiverHomo: An Integrated and Interactive Human Liver Single-Cell Atlas with Protein Interaction and Cell-Cell Communication Networks
abstract: LiverHomo is an integrated cell atlas developed from publicly available human liver single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) datasets spanning healthy and diverse liver disease contexts. While several single-cell resources for the human liver are available, LiverHomo provides broad disease coverage and extends transcriptomic exploration through the integration of protein-protein interaction (PPI) networks and cell-cell interactions. LiverHomo provides an interactive web portal (https://liverhomo.org) for exploring cellular composition, gene expression, differentially expressed genes, Gene Ontology annotations, cell-cell interactions, and context-specific PPI networks across diseases and cell types. To facilitate intuitive access to these multidimensional data, the portal incorporates Ask LiverHomo, a natural-language assistant that interprets user queries and directs users to relevant analyses and visualizations. Interactive histograms, violin plots, network visualizations, and metadata exploration enable users to examine the atlas at cellular, transcriptomic, and protein-interaction levels, while the underlying data are readily accessible for further analysis. Together, LiverHomo provides an integrated and accessible resource for investigating cellular and molecular alterations across human liver health and disease.

title: Multi-method Machine-Learning Identification of IL11 as a Key Gene in Kidney Stone Disease: Mechanistic Clues and Diagnostic Potential.
abstract: Randall's plaque (RP) is a key initiating lesion of idiopathic calcium stones at the renal papilla, and transcriptomic profiling of human RP has revealed inflammation- and matrix-remodeling-related changes, including upregulation of interleukin 11 (IL11). However, under a pure kidney-stone phenotype, a rigorous framework combining multi-algorithm consensus screening with fuller diagnostic appraisal (calibration, internal validation, and decision-curve analysis (DCA)) remains needed. GSE73680 (RP, n=29; normal papilla, n=33) was obtained from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO). Exploratory differential expression (limma) and weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) were intersected, followed by Gene Ontology (GO)/Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) enrichment and Search Tool for the Retrieval of Interacting Genes/Proteins (STRING) protein-protein interaction (PPI) analysis. Consensus genes were defined by five feature-selection algorithms: least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO), support vector machine recursive feature elimination (SVM-RFE), random forest, XGBoost, and Boruta. For IL11, we assessed expression, built a penalized logistic nomogram with receiver operating characteristic (ROC), calibration, and patient-blocked internal validation, and performed Cell-type Identification by Estimating Relative Subsets of RNA Transcripts (CIBERSORT) deconvolution and correlation-ranked KEGG gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA). The intersection of 39 exploratory differentially expressed genes (DEGs) with the WGCNA green module yielded 23 candidates, of which IL11 was the sole five-method consensus gene and was significantly upregulated in RP (Wilcoxon P=8.9×10⁻⁵). The single-gene model achieved an apparent area under the curve (AUC) of 0.782 (95% confidence interval (CI) 0.663-0.901) and an out-of-bag (OOB) AUC of 0.756. PPI linked IL11 to SPP1 and TNFRSF11B, and GSEA enriched lysosome, cell adhesion molecules, and leukocyte transendothelial migration pathways. Building on prior studies, this work strengthens the evidence chain for IL11 as a priority target under a pure kidney-stone/RP phenotype through five-algorithm consensus, complete diagnostic appraisal, and adhesion/migration-related mechanistic clues.

title: Concentration- and duration-associated transcriptional changes in HepG2 cells following long-term nominal nanomolar PFOA exposure.
abstract: Perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) is a persistent environmental contaminant whose transcriptional effects under prolonged low-dose exposure remain insufficiently characterized. We investigated transcriptomic responses in HepG2 cells exposed to nominal PFOA concentrations of 1, 10, or 100nM for 6- or 12-weeks using RNA-seq, differential expression analysis, Gene Ontology enrichment, gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA), and weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA). No differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were detected at 1nM PFOA at either time point. At 10nM and 100nM PFOA, respectively, 149 and 183 DEGs were identified after 6 weeks, predominantly downregulated, compared with 10 and 56 DEGs after 12 weeks. The 6-week response included induction of immediate-early genes (FOS, EGR1) and repression of transcriptional and developmental regulators. At 12 weeks, six downregulated genes, including FOS, FOSB, and PLA2G2A, were shared between concentrations, with no shared upregulated genes. GSEA showed negative enrichment of transcriptional and developmental gene sets at both time points, whereas protein folding and stress response gene sets were enriched only at 6 weeks. WGCNA identified one dominant concentration-associated module at 6 weeks and several smaller modules at 12 weeks, most showing preservation across exposure durations. Together, these findings demonstrate concentration- and duration-associated transcriptional differences following prolonged nanomolar PFOA exposure, while the underlying biological mechanisms and potential contributions of culture-associated changes require further investigation.

title: MIF promotes the progression of breast cancer by combining with CD74 to drive macrophage M2 polarization.
abstract: Breast cancer (BRCA) is one of the most prevalent malignancies in women. Macrophage migration inhibitory factor (MIF) and its receptor CD74 molecule (CD74) have been implicated in tumor immunity, yet their functional interplay within the BRCA microenvironment remains unclear. Transcriptomic datasets and single-cell RNA sequencing analyses were performed to assess the expression patterns, prognostic significance, and cellular localization of MIF and CD74. Their functional interactions were further investigated using an in vitro co-culture system of MCF7 BRCA cells and macrophages, combined with MIF inhibition and CD74 blockade. MIF and CD74 were significantly upregulated in BRCA and associated with poor prognosis. Single-cell analysis showed that CD74 was predominantly expressed in tumor-associated macrophages, whereas MIF was mainly produced by cancer cells. Tumor-derived MIF promoted M2 macrophage polarization through CD74-mediated activation of the phosphoinositide 3-kinase (PI3K)/protein kinase B (AKT) signaling pathway, and this effect was abolished upon disruption of this signaling axis. Hypoxia was identified as a critical upstream regulator driving MIF secretion. These findings identify a hypoxia-driven MIF/CD74 signaling axis that promotes immunosuppressive macrophage polarization in BRCA, highlighting its potential as a therapeutic target.

title: From bench to bedside: translational advances, therapeutic targets, and delivery strategies in diabetic retinopathy.
abstract: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is a leading cause of preventable blindness in adults of working age. Anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) therapy is the reference standard for diabetic macular edema (DME), yet in randomized cohorts, approximately 30-40% of DME eyes still show central macular thickening after six months of continuous treatment. In proliferative DR (PDR), the corresponding limitation is recurrence after treatment interruption rather than primary non-response, and these two patterns should not be conflated. This review examines translational research in DR across four domains. First, we review mechanistic work on the neurovascular unit, metabolic memory and its epigenetic substrate, the gut-retina axis, and human platforms including induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived retinal organoids and clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats (CRISPR) editing. Second, we discuss therapeutic targets beyond VEGF, including the nucleotide-binding oligomerization domain-like receptor family pyrin domain-containing 3 (NLRP3) inflammasome and related inflammatory pathways, neuroprotection, complement activation, the angiopoietin-2 (Ang2)/Tie2 axis, and non-coding RNA (ncRNA) networks. Third, in preclinical pharmacology, we regard delivery as the rate-limiting step and analyze in detail why lipid nanoparticle and N-acetylgalactosamine (GalNAc) conjugation strategies, which transformed hepatic RNA interference, have not translated to the retina, and what the terminated bevasiranib, PF-04523655, and iCo-007 programmes imply for trial design. Fourth, clinical translation, including cytokine biomarkers, artificial intelligence (AI)-based screening, combination regimens, and sustained-release implants. Evidence derived from age-related macular degeneration (AMD), including complement inhibition, stem cell transplantation, and photovoltaic implants, is evaluated separately, and its transferability to DR is assessed in light of differences in affected compartment, pathogenic driver, patient age, and expected treatment duration. We conclude that the principal obstacles in DR are no longer mechanistic but concern cell-type-specific delivery, early-phase trial design, and endpoint standardization, and we specify the evidence each candidate class should generate before clinical development proceeds.

title: AC104024.2/miR-30a-5p Axis Regulates Malignant Progression of Breast Cancer Through a Depression-Related Gene, MAP2K3.
abstract: Breast cancer (BC), a malignant tumor, is characterized by high incidence and poor prognosis among women worldwide. Long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs) and microRNAs (miRNAs) can regulate the initiation and progression of BC through competitive endogenous RNA (ceRNA) mechanisms. Despite depression being an important factor affecting patients with BC, the ceRNA regulatory network involving depression-related genes in BC remains unclear. In this study, we explored the role of the AC104024.2/miR-30a-5p axis in BC progression by targeting the depression-related gene mitogen-activated protein kinase kinase 3 (MAP2K3). We used depression-like mouse models to confirm the role of MAP2K3 in modulating depressive behavior. Additionally, gene set enrichment analyses (GSEA) and phenotypic experiments were conducted to verify the effects of the AC104024.2/miR-30a-5p/MAP2K3 axis on BC cell proliferation, migration, and apoptosis. Luciferase reporter assays were performed to demonstrate the ceRNA function of AC104024.2 for miR-30a-5p. Our results showed that the AC104024.2/miR-30a-5p axis promotes the malignant progression of BC by regulating MAP2K3. In depression-like mouse models, MAP2K3 was identified as a key gene modulating depressive behavior. The AC104024.2/miR-30a-5p/MAP2K3 axis significantly influenced BC cell proliferation, migration, and apoptosis. Luciferase reporter assays confirmed that AC104024.2 acts as a ceRNA for miR-30a-5p, thereby affecting MAP2K3 expression. Rescue experiments suggested that the regulatory effects of AC104024.2 on BC malignancy are at least partly dependent on MAP2K3. This study uncovered the role of the depression-related ceRNA network in BC progression and identified AC104024.2 and MAP2K3 as potential biomarkers for the diagnosis and treatment of BC. These findings provide significant clinical implications and applications for the management of BC.

title: Host factor IRS4 impairs antitumor efficacy of oncolytic alphavirus via proteasomal viral protein degradation.
abstract: Alphavirus M1, currently in phase I/II clinical trials (NCT07093814), provides a tractable system to define host determinants of oncolytic virus replication and efficacy. Tandem affinity purification-mass spectrometry mapped the nsP2 interactome in HEK293 cells and identified insulin receptor substrate 4 (IRS4) as a host restriction factor. Knockdown and reciprocal overexpression showed that IRS4 suppresses M1 replication and cytolysis without affecting baseline cell viability. Mechanistically, IRS4 engages the nsP23 replicase polyprotein in cells through an interaction interface mapped to the nsP2 C-domain and promotes ubiquitin-dependent proteasomal degradation of nsP23, thereby attenuating nsP3-dependent subgenomic RNA synthesis and viral structural protein production. TCGA profiling revealed heterogeneous IRS4 elevation in subsets of tumors, suggesting that endogenous IRS4 status may influence responses to M1 virotherapy. Across 12 human cancer cell lines, higher IRS4 expression showed a nonsignificant trend toward reduced M1 sensitivity, with higher logIC50 and AUC values. In PC9 and UMUC3 cells, ectopic IRS4 expression impaired M1-mediated killing in vitro and abrogated antitumor efficacy in xenograft models. Together, these findings identify IRS4 as a regulator of M1 replicase stability and support the hypothesis that IRS4 expression may represent a candidate negative biomarker for M1 oncolytic virotherapy.

title: Multi-Omics Insights Into Circulating T-Cell Metabolic Reprogramming and Treg Dysfunction in Moyamoya Disease.
abstract: Moyamoya disease (MMD) is a progressive cerebrovascular disease linked to immune dysregulation, yet T-cell metabolic reprogramming and regulatory T-cell (Treg) function remain poorly understood. Here, we integrated multi-omics approaches, including mass cytometry, single-cell RNA sequencing, bulk RNA sequencing, metabolomics, and flow cytometry to characterize T-cell metabolic alterations and Treg dysfunction in MMD, uncovering a key metabolic-immune axis. Compared with healthy controls, MMD patients showed chronic immune activation and broad suppression of amino acid, glycolytic, and fatty acid metabolic pathways. Although Tregs were aberrantly expanded, they displayed metabolic inflexibility, together with impaired intercellular communication. Single-cell transcriptomics indicated Treg-to-Th17 conversion, while flow cytometry confirmed increased IL-17A+ cells within the CD4+FOXP3+ compartment. Besides, these dysfunctional Tregs correlated with advanced Suzuki stages, ischemic stroke, and posterior cerebral artery involvement. Bulk transcriptomic and serum metabolomic analyses further confirmed coordinated immune activation and metabolic suppression at the gene, protein, pathway, and metabolite levels. These findings define a metabolic-immune axis in MMD in which metabolically constrained, functionally unstable Tregs may contribute to neuroinflammation and vascular remodeling, suggesting that restoring Treg metabolic fitness could represent a therapeutic strategy.

title: Dihydrotanshinone I suppresses ovarian cancer by targeting splicing factor SRSF1 to regulate the long non-coding RNA SLC8A1-AS1/FOXO1 axis.
abstract: Ovarian cancer (OC) is a lethal malignancy with limited therapies. The natural compound dihydrotanshinone I (DHT) exhibits broad antitumor activity, yet its precise molecular targets and mechanistic interplay with oncogenic lncRNAs in OC remain largely unexplored. This study aimed to investigate the molecular targets and underlying mechanisms of DHT‑regulated lncRNAs in OC. DHT efficacy was evaluated in vitro and in vivo. Mechanisms were investigated via lncRNA profiling, transcriptomic analysis, functional assays, and protein‑binding experiments. The antitumor efficacy of DHT was assessed in OC cells and xenograft models. LncRNA candidates were screened using microarray and validated by clinical cohort analysis. The regulatory role of SLC8A1-AS1 was further verified through functional assays. RNA pull-down/MS and RIP were performed to identify proteins binding to SLC8A1-AS1. Rescue experiments were conducted to evaluate whether SRSF1 influences SLC8A1-AS1 stability. The DHT-SRSF1 interaction and binding sites were examined through SPR, CETSA, DARTS, MS, and molecular docking. Transcriptomics and western blot were conducted to analyze downstream signaling cascades. DHT significantly suppressed OC growth. SLC8A1-AS1 was highly expressed and associated with poor prognosis in OC. Mechanistically, SRSF1 bound to SLC8A1-AS1 and enhanced its stability, activating the PI3K/AKT/FOXO1 pathway. DHT directly bound to SRSF1 and induced its degradation, downregulating SLC8A1-AS1 expression and inactivating the pathway, ultimately suppressing proliferation in OC. This study identifies SLC8A1-AS1 as a novel prognostic biomarker in OC and provides the first evidence that DHT exerts its antitumor effects by targeting the SRSF1/SLC8A1-AS1/FOXO1 axis. These findings unveil the role of SLC8A1-AS1 in OC progression and elucidate the mechanistic basis for the therapeutic potential of DHT.

title: Cell-Cell Communication in Embryonic Kidney Development: Insights from Single-Cell and Spatial Transcriptomics.
abstract: Embryonic kidney morphogenesis depends on the coordinated communication among ureteric epithelium, nephron progenitors, stroma, endothelium and differentiating nephrons. Classical studies established central roles for glial cell line-derived neurotrophic factor (GDNF) signaling through the RET proto-oncogene receptor tyrosine kinase (RET), WNT-family signaling, fibroblast growth factor (FGF), bone morphogenetic protein (BMP), Notch, Hedgehog, vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) and platelet-derived growth factor (PDGF) pathways, but pathway-centered models do not fully explain why similar signals produce different outcomes across cell states, anatomical locations and developmental stages. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) and spatial transcriptomics have refined these models by resolving heterogeneous progenitor, stromal and vascular states, reassigning several signal sources and constraining predicted interactions to defined tissue relationships. Here, we examine how these findings change the interpretation of ureteric bud (UB) branching, nephron progenitor transitions, stromal patterning and vascular integration. We use the dynamic developmental niche as an evidence-organizing framework, rather than as a new biological entity, to distinguish established mechanisms from relationships supported mainly by transcriptomic, spatial or computational evidence. Vascular, immune and mechanical interactions are evaluated according to their model-specific support, and we outline experiments required to connect predicted communication with morphogenetic outcomes and congenital anomalies of the kidney and urinary tract (CAKUT).

title: Single-Cell Measurement Revolution: A New Paradigm in Tuberculosis Diagnosis.
abstract: Despite a century of advances in tuberculosis (TB) diagnostics, a deceptively simple question remains unanswered: Can we reliably detect a single viable Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) bacillus in a clinical sample? In this perspective, we examine three complementary single-cell measurement platforms that face significant challenges in addressing this seemingly simple yet exceedingly difficult question. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) can resolve host immune heterogeneity by identifying novel cell subsets and diagnostic biomarkers, such as GBP5, that are otherwise obscured in bulk measurements. Direct Mtb scRNA-seq offers unprecedented insights into four critical biological mechanisms: infectivity, drug resistance, persister formation, and host-pathogen interactions; however, its practical clinical application remains limited. Complementing these genomic approaches, single-cell surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy serves as a spectroscopic platform to capture molecular heterogeneity among individual bacilli, revealing drug-resistance signatures that are typically masked by population-averaged spectra. Furthermore, single-cell fluorescent probes, arguably the most promising approach for ultimately overcoming this challenge, act as chemical measurement platforms. They enable the direct visualization of viable Mtb by leveraging pathogen-specific metabolic, enzymatic, or transport-based fluorescence activations. We critically evaluate existing translational barriers, including inadequate sensitivity across diverse clinical specimens (e.g., sputum, swabs, body fluids, tissues, and breath aerosols) as well as high costs and incompatibility with routine clinical workflows. Looking ahead, we underscore future direction in TB diagnostic measurement science, emphasizing specimen-driven probe design and the critical challenge of distinguishing slow replication-competent bacilli from metabolically active but nonreplicating populations. Collectively, these emerging technologies chart a roadmap toward the ultimate goal of detecting a single viable Mtb bacterium in clinical samples.

title: Precision medicine approaches in diabetic cardiomyopathy: from molecular mechanisms to personalized therapeutic strategies.
abstract: Diabetic cardiomyopathy (DCM) is a distinct myocardial disease defined by the existence of abnormal myocardial structure and performance in diabetes mellitus patients without hypertension and coronary artery disease. DCM has been identified as a major cause of heart failure, hospitalisation and cardiovascular mortality with increasing global burden of diabetes. However, there is a large interindividual variation in disease susceptibility, disease progression and response to therapy, highlighting the limitations of conventional management strategies that are applied uniformly. Precision medicine provides a transformational approach through the integration of genomic, molecular, imaging, clinical and lifestyle data to allow for personalized risk assessment, early diagnosis, prognostication and treatment. This review presents the recent advances in the field of precision medicine for DCM with a focus on the molecular pathological mechanisms including metabolic disorders, oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, inflammation, fibrosis and microvascular injury. We discuss the relevance of genomics, pharmacogenomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics, lipidomics and epigenomics in the context of disease heterogeneity and identification of novel therapeutic targets. Emerging biomarkers including circulating microRNAs, non-coding RNAs, inflammatory mediators, fibrosis-related markers and extracellular vesicles are discussed for their potential in personal diagnosis and prognosis. We also consider the increasing role of advanced cardiac imaging, digital phenotyping, wearable technologies, artificial intelligence, and machine learning in enhancing early detection and clinical decision-making. In this review, the therapeutic advances, including sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors, glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists, anti-fibrotic therapies, mitochondrial-targeted interventions, regenerative medicine, gene therapy, and RNA-based therapeutics, are discussed, with a focus on the precision medicine approach. Finally, we present current challenges in data integration, clinical validation, cost-effectiveness, and ethical issues, and highlight future directions in digital twins, multi-omics integration, and AI-driven personalized cardiology. The combination of these technologies has the potential to revolutionize the prevention and management of diabetic cardiomyopathy and improve cardiovascular outcomes in patients with diabetes.

title: Integrative Transcriptomics and Machine Learning Identify Temporal Stress Signatures and Astrocytic Neurocan Associated With Hypothalamic Injury.
abstract: Stress-related neurological dysfunction evolves dynamically, but molecular markers distinguishing stress stages remain limited. We aimed to characterize temporal hypothalamic transcriptomic changes and identify molecular signatures for stress-stage discrimination. Whole-transcriptome sequencing was performed in mouse hypothalami after stress. Differential expression, temporal clustering, co-expression network analysis, and machine learning were integrated to identify stress-associated mRNA and miRNA signatures. Candidate markers were validated by RT-qPCR and single-nucleus RNA sequencing. Ncan function was further evaluated by protein supplementation, perineuronal net analysis, behavioral testing, and regulatory network analysis. mRNAs exhibited strong temporal sensitivity and captured stage-specific transcriptional remodeling, whereas miRNAs primarily reflected stress regardless of duration. A six-mRNA signature (Ncan, Mt2, Nab2, Ptch1, and Catspere1/Catspere2) accurately distinguished control, acute stress, and chronic stress (accuracy, 1.000), while an 11-miRNA signature robustly classified stress states (accuracy, 0.944). Both signatures were validated by RT-qPCR and nested cross-validation, with accuracies of 0.898 and 0.890, respectively. Ncan was consistently top-ranked, predominantly expressed in astrocytes, progressively downregulated by stress, and its supplementation restored PNNs and alleviated depressive-like behaviors. Virtual Ncan knockout disrupted the stress network, with Ctcf predicted as its upstream regulator. Our study identifies distinct stress-stage and stress-state transcriptomic signatures and highlights astrocytic Ncan as a candidate biomarker that may contribute to stress-induced neural injury by regulating PNN homeostasis.

title: Tumor γδ T-cell abundance is associated with favorable cancer treatment outcomes.
abstract: Clinical response to immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) remains variable. We performed a reference-wide screen to identify immune-cell populations in the tumor microenvironment (TME) associated with benefit across treatment modalities and tumor types. We analyzed pretreatment bulk tumor RNA-seq to identify RNA-abundance patterns associated with favorable outcomes in (1) published ICB cohorts with response labels and (2) pretreatment TCGA cohorts with survival outcomes. To identify associated cell types, we compared favorable expression patterns to previously determined patterns for 157 cell types defined by the Human Primary Cell Atlas (HPCA), spanning immune, stromal, vascular, and epithelial lineages. Cell types were associated with favorable outcomes using Cox models (TCGA survival) and mixed-effects models of responder status that accounted for cohort, therapy class, tumor type (ICB cohorts). ICB analyses were restricted to pretreatment samples. Random-effects meta-analysis was used for the PRECOG cross-platform replication. After γδ T-cells emerged as the top-ranked population associated with ICB response, we adjusted γδ associations for CD8 + T-cell abundance, and evaluated γδ signals with TRUST4-based T-cell receptor gamma (TRG) and delta (TRD) gene reconstruction and single-cell RNA-seq. To test whether ICB-favorable cellular landscapes were shared with non-immunotherapy treatment response, we used TCGA RECIST-evaluable treatment records to derive immune-cell profiles associated with treatment response for chemotherapy, radiation, targeted therapy, and hormone therapy. The γδ T-cell program was the top-ranked cell-type program associated with ICB response and was also among the programs most strongly associated with favorable TCGA survival. Cell types associated with ICB response showed strong descriptive concordance with the chemotherapy-response profile derived from recorded TCGA outcomes (Pearson r of ranks = 0.92) and moderate concordance with the analogous radiation-associated profile (r = 0.58). Analyses of targeted and hormone therapies were limited by small sample sizes and showed weaker concordance. In pretreatment tumor biopsies, inferred γδ T-cell abundance was associated with ICB response and with survival, and these associations were not explained simply by CD8 + T-cell abundance. In TCGA, TRUST4-derived γδ T-cell receptor (TCR) abundance estimates correlated with signature-based γδ scores and stratified survival. In independent single-cell RNA-seq datasets, higher γδ TCR RNA abundance was also associated with a higher rate of ICB response. A reference-wide cell-type screen identified γδ T-cells as the leading population associated with ICB response, and pretreatment γδ T-cell abundance was also associated with favorable outcomes in immunotherapy and non-immunotherapy settings. The evidence is associative and varies in strength by tumor context but supports prospective evaluation of γδ T-cell abundance as a component of pretreatment immune profiling alongside CD8, B-cell/TLS, stromal, and epithelial-state features. Across cancers, clinical response to immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) is variable, with inconsistent performance from established biomarkers such as PD-L1 and tumor mutation burden. We asked which immune-cell transcriptional programs were associated with favorable outcomes across immunotherapy and non-immunotherapy treatment settings. Using pretreatment bulk tumor RNA-seq from published ICB cohorts and TCGA, we evaluated the inferred abundance of 157 subtypes in the tumor microenvironment (TME) with a common gene-level and sample-level framework. Pretreatment TMEs enriched in lymphoid cells or γδ T-cells were associated with ICB response and with favorable survival. The immune-cell landscape associated with favorable ICB outcomes was strongly concordant with chemotherapy response and moderately concordant with radiation response. The association between γδ abundance and favorable outcomes remained after accounting for CD8 + T-cell abundance. These observational findings support γδ T-cell abundance as a candidate for pretreatment immune profiling that warrants prospective evaluation.

title: A pan-cohort transcriptional landscape of breast cancer maps subtype and microenvironmental programs.
abstract: Breast cancer comprises heterogeneous transcriptional states that are incompletely captured by discrete clinical or molecular subtype labels. To visualize this heterogeneity in a unified framework, we integrated bulk RNA-seq data from 2,284 patient samples across 13 studies using 18,089 protein coding genes, a harmonized processing pipeline, batch correction, consensus clustering and PaCMAP dimensionality reduction to construct an interactive breast cancer transcriptional landscape. Consensus clustering identified five major regions, which were annotated using PAM50 scores calculated for each sample: Luminal A, Luminal B, HER2-enriched, and two basal-associated clusters. The basal clusters separated into an immune-rich region marked by T cell-inflamed, tumor-associated macrophages (TAM), and low-purity signatures, and a cell-cycle-driven region enriched for proliferation and DNA replication programs. Overlay of marker genes, pathways, kinases, neuronal-like signaling programs, cancer associated fibroblasts (CAF) states, and TAM programs revealed spatially organized subtype biology and microenvironmental heterogeneity. Finally, projection of therapy-associated resistance signatures identified landscape regions linked to predicted resistance to HER2-targeted therapy and hormone receptor-directed endocrine therapies. By enabling interactive exploration of transcriptional states, marker genes, pathways, and therapeutic response programs, this resource provides a community framework for biomarker discovery in breast cancer. We present a unified, multi-cohort transcriptional landscape of breast cancer that organizes canonical subtypes along continuous biological axes and reveals spatially structured regions of therapeutic sensitivity and resistance. By enabling projection of patient samples and patient-derived models into this framework, we provide a practical tool for interpreting tumor biology and guiding translational discovery. We integrate 13 breast cancer transcriptomic datasets using a harmonized processing pipeline with batch correction and dimensionality reduction to construct a unified landscape spanning basal, HER2-enriched, luminal A, luminal B, and normal-like subtypes. Continuous gradients of proliferation, endocrine signaling, metabolic activity, and tissue architecture organize the space and recapitulate subtype biology. Overlay of clinical outcomes reveals high-risk regions beyond discrete subtype boundaries, while integration of gene expression and copy number alterations links genomic events to pathway-level programs. Microenvironmental features, including cancer-associated fibroblast programs, map to distinct regions of the landscape. Projection of drug response signatures identifies zones of sensitivity and intrinsic resistance. The framework supports embedding of patient samples and patient-derived xenograft models and is available as an interactive resource for exploration and projection of new datasets. A landscape built using only transcriptomic analysis for breast cancer reveals novel insights about subtype-specific biology.

title: Multi-Dataset Transcriptomic Screening Identifies Myosin VI as a Prognostic Biomarker Linked to Migration in Prostate Cancer.
abstract: Distant metastasis remains a principal determinant of mortality in prostate cancer (PCa), yet markers associated with metastatic potential at an early stage remain scarce. Here, cross-cohort mining of public transcriptomic data was combined with in vitro loss-of-function experiments to nominate and characterize candidate prognostic and metastasis-associated markers in PCa. Six independent cohorts-the Cancer Genome Atlas prostate adenocarcinoma cohort (TCGA-PRAD) and five Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) series-were analyzed separately for differential expression between tumor and adjacent normal tissue, with Benjamini-Hochberg control of the false discovery rate (FDR) applied within each dataset before cross-dataset comparison. This analysis identified 81 consensus differentially expressed genes (DEGs). Candidates were prioritized by protein-protein interaction (PPI) network analysis, weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), and exploratory Kaplan-Meier survival screening. The two leading genes were re-examined using the Tumor Immune Estimation Resource (TIMER) database, where only myosin VI (MYO6) remained associated with shorter overall survival (hazard ratio [HR] = 2.35, P = 0.0385). Lentiviral short hairpin RNA (shRNA) silencing of MYO6 in PC-3 and DU145 cells reduced migration and invasion, whereas colony-formation and MTS assays showed a concurrent increase in proliferation, a dissociation compatible with a "go-or-grow" trade-off. Immunoblotting after MYO6 silencing showed higher E-cadherin and Claudin-1 and lower N-cadherin, whereas Vimentin changed in the opposite direction, indicating a partial rather than complete epithelial shift. These findings identify MYO6 as a prognostic and metastasis-associated candidate in PCa and support the broader applicability of this screening framework for biomarker nomination in other tumor types.

title: An osteogenic microenvironment improves response during denosumab treatment in giant cell tumors of bone in the spine.
abstract: Giant cell tumors of bone are benign but locally aggressive tumors. Typically diagnosed in individuals between the ages of 20 and 40 years, these tumors cause significant amounts of pain, and morbidity. Giant cell tumors of bone can be treated with an increased dosing regimen of denosumab, a monoclonal antibody that targets receptor activator of nuclear kappa-B ligand, which has shown promise in reducing pain and tumor size, while contributing to improved ossification of the tumor. However, the ossification response observed varies, with some patients responding rapidly with total tumor ossification, while others respond slowly, if at all. Due to gaps in our current understanding of what improves ossification in patients, we aimed to identify patient specific biomarkers that contributed to increased ossification in our patient cohort. Pre-treatment biopsy samples from 19 patients collected from 3 North American centres were grouped based on their response to denosumab, determined from their change in Boriani ossification grade after treatment. The 19 patients pre-treatment tissue was used in gene expression analysis using RNA extraction and nanoString analysis. A subset of tissue from 6 patients and 3 healthy controls were included in protein expression analysis, where differential expression and gene set enrichment analysis was conducted to identify upregulated proteins and pathways contributing to the different treatment responses. A distinct microenvironment was identified through both genetic and proteomic expression. Good responders demonstrated upregulation of TNFRSF11B and CX3CL1, genes that are related to bone remodeling, and a downregulation of CX3CR1. Additionally, tissue remodeling and cell proliferation markers were upregulated, while immune related markers were downregulated in our good responders (increased ossification of tumor). Genetic analysis was complemented by protein analysis which in our good responders demonstrated upregulation of bone pathways associated with bone development, bone mineralization, ossification, and osteoblast differentiation, and downregulation in bone remodeling, bone resorption, and osteoclast differentiation. Further analysis identified upregulation of LTF, FBLN5, LOX, CHAD, and OGN, and downregulation of CEBPB, CTSK, and TFRC. Giant cell tumors of bone show varied mineralization responses to denosumab, with the biological factors associated with this variability remaining poorly understood. We used gene and protein expression analysis of pre-treatment biopsy tissue to compare good and poor mineralization responses. The good responders demonstrate a pre-treatment tumor microenvironment that favors bone formation and reduced resorption, suggesting that biomarker analysis of biopsied samples may help to understand a patient's response to denosumab and guide personalized treatment strategies.

title: scGlycoAI: Machine learning analysis of single-cell glycan and RNA sequencing data for cell-type annotation and malignancy-associated glycan discovery.
abstract: Single-cell glycan and RNA sequencing (scGR-seq) enables characterization of cellular glycan heterogeneity. Here, we present scGlycoAI, an interpretable machine learning framework that integrates scGR-seq data for glycan-centered biological discovery. Using lectin-binding profiles as input, scGlycoAI employs hierarchical machine learning to accurately classify cell types and subtypes within complex tumor microenvironments. Applied to pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) datasets, scGlycoAI achieved an overall eight-class classification accuracy of 90.3% under leave-one-patient-out validation using glycan features alone. These results demonstrate that glycan signatures, despite their lower dimensionality compared with transcriptomic profiles, are sufficient for robust cell-type annotation and represent cell-type-specific molecular signatures. Feature importance analysis identified PVL lectin binding, which reflects recognition of sialylated and/or GlcNAc-containing glycans, as a key feature of aggressive cancer states. A neural-network model combined with SHAP-based interpretation further revealed that elevated PVL binding was associated with transcriptional programs linked to epithelial-mesenchymal transition, KRAS signaling, extracellular matrix remodeling, and inflammatory responses. Higher expression of the PVL-associated gene signature was associated with poorer overall survival in the TCGA pancreatic adenocarcinoma cohort. Collectively, these findings suggest that glycan-based machine learning enables accurate cell classification while providing biological insights into malignancy-associated glycan states at single-cell resolution. This framework provides a foundation for glycan-centered biomarker discovery and glycan-targeted therapeutic development.

title: Basic leucine zipper ATF-like transcription factor (BATF) as a candidate marker associated with venous thromboembolism risk factors in sepsis: an integrated bioinformatics and machine learning analysis.
abstract: Sepsis affects over 19 million people worldwide annually and is associated with an increased risk of venous thromboembolism (VTE), which significantly worsens clinical outcomes. However, current biomarkers such as D-dimer lack specificity, and the molecular signatures associated with VTE risk in sepsis remain unclear. We applied integrative transcriptomics and machine learning approaches to identify VTE-associated biomarkers in sepsis-related datasets. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), differential gene expression analysis, and immune infiltration assessments were conducted using publicly available datasets. Candidate biomarkers were further evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, Cox regression, nomogram modeling, single-cell RNA sequencing, and quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR) validation. Basic leucine zipper ATF-like transcription factor (BATF) emerged as a top candidate biomarker, significantly associated with both sepsis and VTE-related datasets (fold change >1.5, p < 0.001). BATF expression showed consistent elevation across multiple independent cohorts and demonstrated discriminatory performance for disease- or risk-score-defined phenotypes, with area under the curve (AUC) values ranging from 0.831 to 0.953. High BATF expression was associated with prolonged prothrombin time and 28-day mortality in sepsis patients (p = 0.024). Single-cell analysis showed BATF enrichment in macrophages and dendritic cells. BATF may serve as a candidate biomarker associated with high VTE risk phenotypes and 28-day mortality in sepsis-related cohorts. However, BATF was not validated against adjudicated or imaging-confirmed VTE events in this study; therefore, it should not be interpreted as a diagnostic marker for confirmed VTE or a direct predictor of thrombosis. Prospective cohorts with adjudicated VTE outcomes are required to confirm its clinical utility.
